- Gateway: expose `gateway.handshakeTimeoutMs` in config, schema, and docs while preserving `OPENCLAW_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_MS` precedence, so loaded or low-powered hosts can tune local WebSocket pre-auth handshakes without patching dist files. Supersedes #51282; refs #73592 and #73652. Thanks @henry-the-frog.
- Gateway/TUI/status: align configured and env-based WebSocket handshake budgets across local clients, probes, and fallback RPCs while preserving explicit status timeouts and paired-device auth fallback, so slow local gateways are not marked unreachable by a shorter client watchdog. Refs #73524, #73535, #73592, and #73602. Thanks @harshcatsystems-collab, @DJBlackhawk, and @Vksh07.
- Gateway/startup: return retryable `UNAVAILABLE` during the sidecar startup window and keep CLI/TUI/status clients retrying inside their existing timeout budget, so early connects no longer surface as terminal handshake failures. Fixes #73652. Thanks @spenceryang1996-dot.
- Gateway/proxy: bypass inherited proxy environment for local Gateway control-plane WebSockets to `localhost` as well as loopback IPs, so Windows/WSL proxy settings cannot intercept local CLI/TUI Gateway connections. Supersedes #73474; refs #73602. Thanks @DhtIsCoding.
- Doctor/Gateway: use a lightweight `status` RPC without channel summary work for doctor Gateway liveness, so slow health snapshots do not falsely drive service restart repair. Fixes #64400; supersedes #64511. Thanks @CHE10X and @EronFan.
- Agents/auth: scope external CLI credential discovery to configured providers during model auth status and startup prewarm, so opencode-only and other single-provider gateways do not block on unrelated Claude CLI Keychain probes. Fixes #73908. Thanks @Ailuras.
- Agents/model selection: resolve slash-form aliases before provider/model parsing and keep alias-resolved primary models subject to transient provider cooldowns, so cron and persisted sessions do not retry cooled-down raw aliases. Fixes #73573 and #73657. Thanks @akai-shuuichi and @hashslingers.
- Agents/Claude CLI: reuse already-cached macOS Keychain credentials for no-prompt Claude credential reads, so doctor/runtime checks do not miss fresh interactive Claude auth. Fixes #73682. Thanks @RyanSandoval.
- Agents/Claude CLI doctor: scope workspace and project-dir checks to agents that actually use the Claude CLI runtime, so non-default Claude agents no longer make the default agent look Claude-backed. Fixes #73903. Thanks @bobfreeman1989.
- Gateway/sessions: expose effective agent runtime metadata on session rows, `sessions.patch`, and local `openclaw sessions --json`, while keeping Claude CLI-backed rows on the canonical model provider so runtime backend and model identity are no longer conflated. Fixes #73090. Thanks @vishutdhar.
- Gateway/auth status: scope external CLI credential overlays to configured providers, runtimes, or profiles and keep status reads off new Keychain prompts, so single-provider Gateway configs no longer probe unrelated Claude/Codex/MiniMax auth on startup. Fixes #73908. Thanks @Ailuras.
- Agents/runtime status: expose effective agent runtime metadata in `agents.list`, Control UI agent panels, and `/agents`, and avoid rendering stale or cumulative CLI token totals as live context usage. Fixes #73660, #73578, and #45268. Thanks @spartman, @DashLabsDev, and @xyooz.
- Agents/transcripts: strip empty assistant text blocks while preserving valid text, images, and signatures, so Anthropic-style providers no longer reject sanitized transcript turns. Fixes #73640. Thanks @jowhee327.
- Gateway/sessions: preserve session keys on hidden lifecycle events so channel-routed runs still persist terminal session state and do not strand session status as running after Codex turn completion. Thanks @cathrynlavery.
- Providers/Bedrock: omit deprecated `temperature` for Claude Opus 4.7 Bedrock model ids, named and application inference profiles, including dotted `opus-4.7` refs, and classify the nested validation response for failover. Fixes #73663. Thanks @bstanbury.
- Gateway: raise the preauth/connect-challenge timeout to 15s so cold CLI starts on slower hosts have more time to process the WebSocket challenge before the Gateway closes the connection. Fixes #51469; refs #73592 and #62060. Thanks @GothicFox and @jackychen-png.
- CLI/status: fall back to a bounded local `status` RPC when loopback detail probes time out or report unknown capability, so reachable local gateways are no longer marked unreachable by slow read diagnostics. Fixes #73535; refs #48360, #62762, #51357, and #42019. Thanks @RacecarGuy, @justinschille, @DJBlackhawk, @tianyaqpzm, and @0xrsydn.
- CLI/gateway: reuse cached paired-device auth during `gateway probe` and report post-connect diagnostic failures as degraded reachability, so healthy local gateways are no longer marked unreachable after loopback auth or read timeouts. Fixes #48360. Thanks @RacecarGuy.
- Channels/Discord: give Discord Gateway WebSocket handshakes a 30s timeout so stalled TLS/network transitions emit an error and Carbon can continue its reconnect loop instead of leaving the bot silent until restart. Refs #50046. Thanks @codexGW.
- Mattermost/WebSocket: send protocol ping/pong keepalives and terminate stale sessions when pongs stop arriving, so silent TCP drops reconnect instead of leaving monitoring idle. Fixes #41837; carries forward #57621; refs #50138, #44160, and #51104. Thanks @JasonWang1124.
- Channels/Telegram: suppress standalone failed edit/write warning payloads when a user-facing assistant error reply already covers the turn, while keeping unresolved mutating failures visible behind success-looking or suppressed-error replies. Fixes #39631; refs #73750; carries forward #39636 and #39717; leaves #39406 for configurable delivery policy. Thanks @Bartok9 and @Bortlesboat.
- Control UI/agents: persist the Set Default action through `agents.list[].default` instead of writing the unsupported `agents.defaultId` field, so saved default-agent changes survive config validation. Fixes #65565; carries forward #72585. Thanks @luyao618.
- NVIDIA/NIM: persist the `NVIDIA_API_KEY` provider marker and mark bundled NVIDIA Chat Completions models as string-content compatible, so NIM models load from `models.json` and OpenAI-compatible subagent calls send plain text content. Fixes #73013 and #50107; refs #73014. Thanks @bautrey, @iot2edge, @ifearghal, and @futhgar.
- Channels/Discord: let text-only configs drop the `GuildVoiceStates` gateway intent and expose a bounded `/gateway/bot` metadata timeout with rate-limited fallback logs, reducing idle CPU and warning floods. Fixes #73709 and #73585. Thanks @sanchezm86 and @trac3r00.
- Agents/sessions: mark same-turn `sessions_send` and A2A reply prompts with an inter-session `isUser=false` envelope before they reach the model, so foreign session output no longer lands as bare active user text. Fixes #73702; refs #73698, #73609, #73595, and #73622. Thanks @alvelda.
- Channels/Telegram: fail closed when account-level public DM settings conflict with a restrictive top-level `allowFrom`, and require an effective wildcard before `dmPolicy="open"` behaves as public access. Fixes #73756; refs #73698. Thanks @Hilo-Hilo and @xace1825.
- Channels/security: move open-DM allowlist semantics into the shared policy helpers and align Discord, Slack, Mattermost, Matrix, Feishu, LINE, IRC, Google Chat, Zalo, Zalo User, QQ Bot, and Synology Chat so `dmPolicy="open"` is public only with an effective wildcard and otherwise still respects sender allowlists. Refs #73756 and #73698. Thanks @Hilo-Hilo and @xace1825.
- ACP/tasks: sweep orphaned parent-owned ACP sessions whose task records are gone, preserving bound persistent sessions but clearing unbound stale ACPX metadata so old child sessions cannot silently respawn into chat. Fixes #73609. Thanks @joerod26.
- Outbound/security: strip known internal runtime scaffolding such as `<system-reminder>` and `<previous_response>` at the final channel delivery boundary and keep Discord output on targeted tag stripping, so degraded harness replies cannot leak those tags to users. Fixes #73595. Thanks @gabrielexito-stack and @martingarramon.
- Security/Telegram: load Telegram security adapters in read-only audit/doctor, audit malformed Telegram DM `allowFrom` entries even when groups are disabled, and keep allowlist DM audits from counting stale pairing-store senders, so public/shared-DM risk checks stay accurate. Refs #73698. Thanks @xace1825.
- Plugins: remove hidden manifest, provider-owner, bootstrap, and channel metadata caches so plugin installs, manifest edits, and bundled-root changes are visible on the next metadata read while keeping runtime/module loader caches for actual plugin code. Thanks @shakkernerd.
- CLI/plugins: use plugin metadata snapshots for install slot selection and add opt-in plugin lifecycle timing traces, so plugin install avoids runtime-loading the plugin registry for metadata-only decisions. Thanks @shakkernerd.
- fix(plugins): restrict bundled plugin dir resolution to trusted package roots. (#73275) Thanks @pgondhi987.
- fix(security): prevent workspace PATH injection via service env and trash helpers. (#73264) Thanks @pgondhi987.
- Active Memory: allow `allowedChatTypes` to include explicit portal/webchat sessions and classify `agent:...:explicit:...` session keys before opaque session ids can shadow the chat type. Fixes #65775. (#66285) Thanks @Lidang-Jiang.
- Active Memory: allow the hidden recall sub-agent to use both `memory_recall` and the legacy `memory_search`/`memory_get` memory tool contract, so bundled `memory-lancedb` recall works without breaking the default `memory-core` path. Fixes #73502. (#73584) Thanks @Takhoffman.
- fix(device-pairing): validate callerScopes against resolved token scopes on repair [AI]. (#72925) Thanks @pgondhi987.
- Active Memory docs: document the `cacheTtlMs` 1000-120000 ms range and 15000 ms default so setup snippets do not lead users past the schema limit. Fixes #65708. (#65737) Thanks @WuKongAI-CMU.
- fix(agents): canonicalize provider aliases in byProvider tool policy lookup [AI]. (#72917) Thanks @pgondhi987.
- fix(security): block npm_execpath injection from workspace .env [AI-assisted]. (#73262) Thanks @pgondhi987.
- Tools/web_fetch: decode response bodies from raw bytes using declared HTTP, XML, or HTML meta charsets before extraction, so Shift_JIS and other legacy-charset pages no longer return mojibake. Fixes #72916. Thanks @amknight.
- Active Memory: skip payload-less `memory_search` transcript tool results when building debug telemetry, so newer empty entries no longer hide the latest useful debug payload. (#68773) Thanks @SimbaKingjoe.
- Active Memory: keep recall setup time from consuming the configured model timeout while giving the hook runner an explicit bounded budget for the plugin, so slow embedded-run setup no longer causes immediate recall timeouts. Fixes #72606. (#72620) Thanks @hyspacex.
- Channels/Discord: bound message read/search REST calls, route those actions through Gateway execution, and fall back to `CommandTargetSessionKey` for inbound hook session keys so Discord reads do not hang and hooks still fire when `SessionKey` is empty. Fixes #73431. (#73521) Thanks @amknight.
- Plugins/media: auto-enable provider plugins referenced by `agents.defaults.imageGenerationModel`, `videoGenerationModel`, and `musicGenerationModel` primary/fallback refs, so configured Google and MiniMax media providers do not stay disabled behind a restrictive plugin allowlist. Thanks @vincentkoc.
- Memory-core/dreaming: retry managed dreaming cron registration after startup when the cron service is not reachable yet, so the scheduled Memory Dreaming Promotion sweep recovers without waiting for heartbeat traffic. Fixes #72841. Thanks @amknight.
- Acpx/runtime: validate the runtime session mode at the `AcpxRuntime.ensureSession` wrapper boundary so callers that pass anything other than `persistent` or `oneshot` get a clear `ACP_INVALID_RUNTIME_OPTION` error instead of silently round-tripping through the encoded handle as a default `persistent` mode and later throwing `SessionResumeRequiredError`. Investigation context: #73071. (#73548) Thanks @amknight.
- CLI/infer: keep web-search fallback on missing provider API keys, preserve structured validation errors from the selected provider, and let per-request image describe prompts override configured media-entry prompts. (#63263) Thanks @Spolen23.
- Chat commands: include configured model-catalog reasoning metadata when building `/think` argument menus so Ollama Cloud and other provider-owned reasoning models show supported levels instead of only `off`. Fixes #73515; supersedes #73568. Thanks @danielzinhu99 and @neeravmakwana.
- Channels/Telegram: suppress generic tool-progress chatter when preview streaming is off, so non-streaming Telegram turns only deliver final replies while approvals, media, and errors still route normally. Refs #72363 and #72482. Thanks @neeravmakwana and @SweetSophia.
- CLI/model probes: add repeatable image `--file` inputs to `infer model run` for local and gateway multimodal model smokes, so vision models such as Ollama Qwen VL and Gemini can be tested through the raw model-probe surface. Fixes #63700. Thanks @cedricjanssens.
- CLI/model probes: request trusted operator scope for `infer model run --gateway --model <provider/model>` so Gateway raw model smokes can use one-off provider/model overrides instead of being rejected before provider auth resolution. Fixes #73759. Thanks @chrislro.
- CLI/image describe: pass `--prompt` and `--timeout-ms` through `infer image describe` and `describe-many`, so custom vision instructions and slow local model budgets reach media-understanding providers such as Ollama, OpenAI, Google, and OpenRouter. Refs #63700. Thanks @cedricjanssens.
- Model selection: include the rejected provider/model ref and allowlist recovery hint when a stored session override is cleared, so local model selections such as Gemma GGUF variants do not fall back to the default with a generic message. Refs #71069. Thanks @CyberRaccoonTeam.
- OpenAI-compatible providers: drop malformed event-only or blank-data SSE frames before the OpenAI SDK stream parser sees them, so proxies that split `event:` from `data:` no longer crash streaming runs with `Unexpected end of JSON input`. Fixes #52802. Thanks @LyHug.
- Gateway/OpenAI-compatible streaming: strip `<final>` tags split across streamed model deltas before they reach SSE clients, so `/v1/chat/completions` no longer emits tag remnants or drops content when final-answer wrappers cross chunk boundaries. Fixes #63325. Thanks @tzwickl.
- Ollama: resolve explicitly selected signed-in `:cloud` models through `/api/show` when `/api/tags` omits them, so working models such as `gemini-3-flash-preview:cloud` and `deepseek-v4-pro:cloud` do not fail dynamic model resolution before the native `/api/chat` transport runs. Fixes #73909. Thanks @chtse53.
- Discord/exec approvals: keep the local `/approve` prompt when no native Discord approval runtime is active, and send a manual fallback notice when native approval delivery reaches no targets, so failed DM cards no longer leave approval turns silent or dependent on model-written shell commands. Fixes #73954; carries forward #74027. Thanks @guarismo and @brokemac79.
- Local model prompt caching: keep stable Project Context above volatile channel/session prompt guidance and stop embedding current channel names in the message tool description, so Ollama, MLX, llama.cpp, and other prefix-cache backends avoid avoidable full prompt reprocessing across channel turns. Fixes #40256; supersedes #40296. Thanks @rhclaw and @sriram369.
- Gateway/OpenAI-compatible API: guard provider policy lookup against runtime providers with non-array `models` values, so `/v1/chat/completions` no longer fails with `provider?.models?.some is not a function`. Fixes #66744; carries forward #66761. Thanks @MightyMoud, @MukundaKatta.
- WhatsApp/Web: pass explicit Baileys socket timings into every WhatsApp Web socket and expose `web.whatsapp.*` keepalive, connect, and query timeout settings so unstable networks can avoid repeated 408 disconnect and opening-handshake timeout loops. Fixes #56365. (#73580) Thanks @velvet-shark.
- WhatsApp/Web: recover recently active listeners when a post-408 reconnect keeps receiving transport frames but stops delivering app messages, while keeping group metadata fallback off Baileys sends. Fixes #63855 and #66920; refs #7433, #67986, #70856, #60007, and #72621. Thanks @legonhilltech-jpg, @octopuslabs-fl, @Kanorin-chan, and @stuswan.
- Channels/Telegram: persist native command metadata on target sessions so topic, helper, and ACP-bound slash commands keep their session metadata attached to the routed conversation. (#57548) Thanks @GaosCode.
- Channels/native commands: keep validated native slash command replies visible in group chats while preserving explicit owner allowlists for command authorization. (#73672) Thanks @obviyus.
- Pairing/doctor: bootstrap `commands.ownerAllowFrom` from the first approved DM pairing when no command owner exists, and have doctor explain missing owners so privileged slash commands are not accidentally unusable after onboarding. Thanks @pashpashpash.
- Telegram/exec: infer native exec approvers from `commands.ownerAllowFrom` and auto-enable the Telegram approval client when an owner is resolvable, so owner-only commands such as `/diagnostics` can be approved in Telegram without duplicate per-channel approver config. Thanks @pashpashpash.
- Auto-reply/session: carry the tail of user/assistant turns into the freshly-rotated transcript on silent in-reply session resets (compaction failure, role-ordering conflict) so direct-chat continuity survives the rebind. Fixes #70853. (#70898) Thanks @neeravmakwana.
- Skills: load grouped skill directories such as `skills/<group>/<skill>/SKILL.md` from configured skill roots while keeping grouped discovery capped for large directories. Fixes #56915. (#72534) Thanks @ottodeng, @MoerAI, and @i010542.
- Config: skip malformed non-string `env.vars` entries before env-reference checks, so config loading no longer crashes on JSON values like numbers or booleans. (#42402) Thanks @MiltonHeYan.
- Docker Compose: default missing config and workspace bind mounts to `${HOME:-/tmp}/.openclaw` so manual compose runs do not create invalid empty-source volume specs. (#64485) Thanks @jlapenna.
- Agents/context engines: preserve the child agent's configured `agentDir` when subagent cleanup re-resolves a context engine, so `onSubagentEnded` hooks keep operating on the correct per-agent state. (#67243) Thanks @jarimustonen.
- Channels/WhatsApp: restrict pairing verification replies to real inbound user content, preventing unsolicited prompts from receipts, typing indicators, presence updates, and other non-message Baileys upserts. Fixes #73797. (#73823) Thanks @hclsys.
- Configure/Ollama: show the configured Ollama model allowlist after Cloud only or Cloud + Local setup and skip slow per-model cloud metadata fetches. (#73995) Thanks @obviyus.
- Channels/WhatsApp: detect explicit group `@mentions` again when the bot's own E.164 is in `allowFrom`, so shared-number setups no longer skip group pings that directly mention the bot. Fixes #49317. (#73453) Thanks @juan-flores077.
- WhatsApp/reliability: publish real transport-liveness into WhatsApp channel status and force earlier reconnects on silent transport stalls, so quiet healthy sessions stay connected while wedged sockets recover before the later remote 408 path. (#72656) Thanks @Sathvik-1007.
- Core/channels: tighten selected runtime, media, and plugin edge-case handling while preserving existing behavior. Thanks @jesse-merhi.
- Channels/WhatsApp: strip leaked plural tool-call XML wrappers on every WhatsApp-visible outbound path and keep channel error payloads out of WhatsApp chats. (#71830) Thanks @rubencu.
- Agents/embedded-runner: inject the resolved OAuth bearer (and forward the run abort signal) on the boundary-aware embedded stream fallback so models that route through `openai-codex-responses` and other boundary-aware transports stop failing with `401 Unauthorized: Missing bearer or basic authentication in header`. Fixes #73559. (#73588) Thanks @openperf.
- Telegram/gateway: bound outbound Bot API calls and cache bundled plugin alias lookup so slow Telegram sends or WSL2 filesystem scans no longer wedge gateway replies. (#74210) Thanks @obviyus.
- Configure/GitHub Copilot: reuse existing Copilot auth during configure and show the provider's manifest model catalog in the model picker. (#74276) Thanks @obviyus.
- Configure/models: keep the model picker scoped to the selected manifest provider and enable its bundled plugin before catalog lookup, so choosing GitHub Copilot no longer falls back to Ollama or skips the catalog. (#74322) Thanks @obviyus.
- Auto-reply/subagents: reject `/focus` from leaf subagents and scope fallback target resolution to the requesting subagent's children, so subagents cannot bind conversations outside their control boundary. (#73613) Thanks @drobison00.
- Gateway/startup: skip inherited workspace startup memory for sandboxed spawned sessions without real-workspace write access, so `/new` no longer preloads host workspace memory into isolated child runs. (#73611) Thanks @drobison00.
- Agents/tool policy: validate caller group IDs against session or spawned context before applying group-scoped tool policies or persisting gateway group metadata, so forged group IDs cannot unlock more permissive tools. (#73720) Thanks @mmaps.
- Commands: keep channel-prefixed owner allowlist entries scoped to matching providers so webchat command contexts cannot inherit external channel owners. Thanks @zsxsoft.
- Auth/device pairing: bound bootstrap handoff token issuance, redemption, and approved pairing baselines to the documented per-role scope allowlist, so bootstrap approvals cannot persistently grant `operator.admin`, `operator.pairing`, or `node.exec` scopes. Thanks @eleqtrizit.
- Providers/GitHub Copilot: support the GUI/RPC wizard device-code auth flow so onboarding from non-TTY clients (gateway RPC bridge, GUI wizards) completes instead of returning empty profiles. Dangerous-state handling now distinguishes `access_denied` and `expired_token` from transport errors. (#73290) Thanks @indierawk2k2.
- Installer/Linux: warn before switching an unwritable npm global prefix to `~/.npm-global`, then tell users to run future global updates with `npm i -g openclaw@latest` without `sudo` so npm keeps using the redirected user prefix. Fixes #44365; carries forward #50479. Thanks @Sayeem3051.
- Gateway/plugins: enable the native `require()` fast path on Windows for bundled plugin modules so plugin loading uses `require()` instead of Jiti's transform pipeline, reducing startup from ~39s to ~2s on typical 6-plugin setups. Fixes #68656. (#74173) Thanks @galiniliev.
- macOS app: detect stale Gateway TLS certificate pins, automatically repair trusted Tailscale Serve rotations, and surface paired-but-disconnected Mac companion nodes so partial Gateway connections no longer look healthy. Thanks @guti.

key_changes: 【Breaking】安全工具配置变更：tools.exec 和 tools.fs 不再隐式扩大受限配置文件范围（messaging/minimal），需显式添加 alsoAllow 条目
Messaging/Automation 增强：新增主动运行引导、可视回复强制、子智能体路由元数据和 heartbeat 提醒的跟进承诺
Memory 系统升级为人员感知 wiki：支持来源视图、对话级 Active Memory 过滤、超时部分召回和 bounded REM 预览诊断

Gateway 可靠性提升：优化慢速主机启动、模型目录重用、事件循环诊断、运行时依赖修复和过期会话恢复

releases.summary:
### Patch Changes

-   c10963d: feat(provider/xai): support non-image file parts (PDF, text, CSV) in the Responses API via `input_file` + `file_url`

    The xAI Responses API accepts `{ type: 'input_file', file_url }` for non-image documents (see <https://docs.x.ai/docs/guides/chat-with-files>), but the AI SDK xAI Responses provider previously threw `UnsupportedFunctionalityError` for any file part whose `mediaType` did not start with `image/`.

    When a file part is passed with `data: URL` and a non-image media type, the provider now emits `{ type: 'input_file', file_url }`. `application/pdf` and `text/*` are also added to `supportedUrls` so the SDK does not download them to bytes before reaching the converter.

    Inline-byte (base64) inputs for non-image media types continue to throw, since xAI's Responses API requires either a public URL or a pre-uploaded `file_id` for non-image documents.

key_changes: 新增支持 PDF、text、CSV 等非图片文件类型的上传功能
通过 `input_file` + `file_url` 方式传递非图片文档
`application/pdf` 和 `text/*` 类型添加到 `supportedUrls`，避免 SDK 下载为字节
修复之前对非图片文件类型错误抛出 `UnsupportedFunctionalityError` 的问题
内联 base64 字节输入仍不支持非图片文件（需使用公共 URL 或预上传 file_id）
ai_summary.summary_cn: xAI Responses Provider 新增对非图片文件（PDF、text、CSV）的支持，现在可以通过 `file_url` 方式传递这些文件类型到 xAI API。对于 PDF 和 text 类型文件，SDK 会直接传递 URL 而不下载到字节。内联 base64 输入仍不支持非图片文件，需使用公共 URL 或预上传的 file_id。

### Patch Changes

-   48f842a: fix(ai): enforce `callOptionsSchema` at runtime in `ToolLoopAgent`

    `ToolLoopAgentSettings.callOptionsSchema` was declared and documented as a runtime schema for `options`, but `tool-loop-agent.ts` never invoked it. Any invariant a developer encoded in the schema was silently bypassed at runtime, and unchecked `options` flowed straight into `prepareCall` and any `instructions` template that interpolated them.

    `ToolLoopAgent.prepareCall` now validates caller-supplied `options` against `callOptionsSchema` (when set) via `safeValidateTypes`, throwing `InvalidArgumentError` on failure before forwarding to `prepareCall` / `generateText` / `streamText`.

releases.author: github-actions[bot]
releases.summary:
### Patch Changes

-   a727da4: chore: ensure consistent import handling and avoid import duplicates or cycles

-   fa6e62b: feat(provider/xai): support non-image file parts (PDF, text, CSV) in the Responses API via `input_file` + `file_url`

    The xAI Responses API accepts `{ type: 'input_file', file_url }` for non-image documents (see <https://docs.x.ai/docs/guides/chat-with-files>), but the AI SDK xAI Responses provider previously threw `UnsupportedFunctionalityError` for any file part whose `mediaType` did not start with `image/`.

    When a file part is passed with `data: URL` and a non-image media type, the provider now emits `{ type: 'input_file', file_url }`. `application/pdf` and `text/*` are also added to `supportedUrls` so the SDK does not download them to bytes before reaching the converter.

    Inline-byte (base64) inputs for non-image media types continue to throw, since xAI's Responses API requires either a public URL or a pre-uploaded `file_id` for non-image documents.

-   Updated dependencies [a727da4]
    -   @ai-sdk/openai-compatible@2.0.43
    -   @ai-sdk/provider-utils@4.0.25
    -   @ai-sdk/provider@3.0.10

key_changes: xAI Responses API 新增支持非图片文件（PDF、text、CSV）上传，通过 `input_file` + `file_url` 实现
当文件包含非图片媒体类型（如 PDF、CSV）时，provider 现在发送 `{ type: 'input_file', file_url }` 格式
`application/pdf` 和 `text/*` 类型文件被添加到 `supportedUrls`，SDK 不会先下载为字节流
内联 base64 格式的非图片文件仍会抛出错误，因为 xAI API 要求非图片文档使用公开 URL 或预上传的 file_id
优化了导入处理逻辑，避免导入重复或循环问题
ai_summary.summary_cn: xAI provider 新增支持在 Responses API 中处理非图片文件（PDF、text、CSV）。当文件 mediaType 不以 `image/` 开头时，现在会通过 `input_file` + `file_url` 方式上传，而非抛出 UnsupportedFunctionivityError。PDF 和 text 类型文件被添加到 supportedUrls，SDK 会直接传递 URL 而不下载到字节流。

issue_insights.summary_brief: 本期共监测到 5 类跨仓库共性问题，影响面最广的是 Python 后端打包缺失（56 仓）和 ACP 云端凭证注入缺陷（19 仓）。单仓层面以 workflow_runtime 缺陷最为密集，累计出现 40+ 个 P0/P1 级信号，其中 Anthropic 全系 SDK（Go/Python/TS）均有严重阻塞问题，多个仓库的会话持久化和工具调用协议存在系统性漏洞。
global_highlights: Python 后端未打包进安装程序已扩散至 56 个下游仓库，导致自主任务功能全面失效，为本期影响面最广的跨仓缺陷
ACP 凭证文件注入方案在云端部署场景下完全不可用，涉及 OpenDevin、AutoGPT、agno 等 19 个仓库的 OAuth 认证链路
Anthropic SDK 家族（Go/Python/TypeScript）集中爆发 omitzero 序列化丢失字段、Vertex AI 端点 404、asyncio 事件循环阻塞等 P0 级缺陷，影响所有消费这些 SDK 的下游项目
DeepSeek V4 reasoning_content 字段未回传问题在 opencode、OpenDevin、ClawX 三仓同时出现，表明多模型思维链 API 兼容存在系统性盲区

source_issues.title: ACP: conversations cannot be resumed after sandbox restart (session_id is not persisted)
source_issues.evidence: Root cause clearly identified: acp_session_id and acp_session_cwd are stored in sandbox LocalFileStore (base_state.json) which is wiped on sandbox recycle; ACP server session files live in sandbox $HOME which is also wiped. Proposed fixes include bootstrap-prompt resume and native session/load persist.

source_issues.title: [Feature]: Support passing reasoning_content back to API for DeepSeek V4 compatibility

top_pain_points.topic: ACP credential file injection not supported for cloud deployments (OAuth-based ACP auth blocked)
top_pain_points.summary: ACP agents (Claude Code, Codex) authenticate via local credential files (~/.claude, ~/.codex) from OAuth login. These files live on the user's machine and are inaccessible in cloud deployments where the backend runs on a different host. Previous local-only implementation cannot copy files from the backend filesystem into the sandbox for cloud users.

top_pain_points.topic: Docker image SIGILL crash on Apple Silicon with podman — cryptography 47.0.0 ARM wheel incompatibility
top_pain_points.summary: Running the Phoenix Docker image (15.0.0) on Apple Silicon via podman causes the container to exit immediately with code 132 (SIGILL — illegal instruction). Root cause: the cryptography 47.0.0 wheel targets ARMv8.2-A+ (with PAC/BTI/SVE2 instructions) which the Apple Hypervisor VM does not correctly implement, causing a crash at .so load time before any Python code runs.

top_pain_points.review_reason: This is a complete startup crash for self-hosted users on Apple Silicon using podman. The Phoenix Docker image is entirely unusable — it crashes before any Python code executes, making the product completely non-functional for this deployment target. Exit code 132 (SIGILL) means illegal CPU instruction, which cannot be worked around without rebuilding or downgrading. Only the 11.14 workaround exists. This directly blocks self-hosted Apple Silicon + podman users from using Phoenix 15.0.0.

source_issues.title: [BUG]: Docker image exits immediately (SIGILL) on Apple Silicon with podman — cryptography 47.0.0 incompatible with Apple Hypervisor VM
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction: podman run arizephoenix/phoenix:latest on Apple Silicon → container exits with code 132 (SIGILL). Verified root cause: cryptography.hazmat.bindings._rust fails to load with illegal instruction at .so load time. The same class of issue is documented in pyca/cryptography#12069. Workaround: use arizephoenix/phoenix:11.14 (cryptography 45.0.5) which ships a manylinux_2_28 wheel compatible with Apple Hypervisor.

source_issues.title: FilesystemBackend re-raises bare OSError, breaks SkillsMiddleware on symlinked SKILL.md
source_issues.evidence: Reproducer: FilesystemBackend with a symlinked SKILL.md raises OSError(ELOOP) instead of returning FileDownloadResponse(error=...). On macOS, Claude Code's ~/.claude/skills are commonly symlinked. With enable_skills=True (default in deepagents-cli), any such symlink aborts the entire agent: 'RemoteException: {error: OSError, message: An internal error occurred}'. signals.topic: Playground replay fails for Anthropic computer_* tool types due to missing beta header
signals.summary: When replaying spans or prompts that include Anthropic computer_20250124/computer_20251124 tool types in the Playground, the request fails with a 400 validation error because Phoenix's Anthropic client does not set the required `anthropic-beta` header (e.g. `computer-use-2025-11-24`). The Messages API validator rejects these tool types as unknown without the header.
aliases: Anthropic computer tool beta header missing
computer_* tool type validation failure in Playground
signals.review_reason: This is a clear main-flow blocking bug. Users cannot use the Playground to replay any span/prompt that includes an Anthropic computer tool — the request is rejected outright with a 400 at the API validation layer before any model call is made. The failure is reproducible and blocks the core LLM Span Replay workflow. Only 1 issue is present in this snapshot but it is a standalone blocking bug with a concrete error and root cause. The same root cause likely affects other beta-gated tools (MCP, advisor-tool) making this a systemic pattern.

source_issues.title: Anthropic computer use tool: Playground rejects computer_* tool types without beta header

Reproduction: save a prompt with a computer tool definition, hit Run in Playground → immediate 400.

The bug is reproducible with a concrete API error message and affects all Anthropic client tools, not just memory.

webui bun lockb incompatible with npm lockfile
signals.review_reason: Every PR preview build fails due to bun resolving incompatible newer package versions. While a temporary workaround exists (wrangler.toml npm pin), the root incompatibility means bun cannot be used for local dev or CI, and the issue surfaces fresh errors on each package update. Count=2 from separate but root-cause-identical reports spanning multiple PRs.

source_issues.title: track(webui): bun has never produced a working build — npm-only is currently enforced via wrangler.toml
source_issues.evidence: Bun resolves newer package versions than package-lock.json, breaking every CF Pages preview build. Observed on PRs #2265, #2247, #2241, #2233 and others. Root cause: @icons-pack/react-simple-icons 13.13.0 removes SiOpenai export; react-hook-form 7.74.0 has stricter types. Workaround (wrangler.toml npm pin) was added but bun support was never fully fixed.

source_issues.title: bug(cf-pages): Cloudflare Pages preview build fails with pre-existing TypeScript errors
source_issues.evidence: Every PR gets a red CF Pages check due to pre-existing TypeScript errors surfaced by bun build but not caught by GH Actions typecheck. Errors TS2724 (SiOpenai) and TS2345 (McpConfiguration) exist on master. Confirmed on PRs #2265, #2247, #2241, #2233.

signals.topic: gptme-server sidecar zombie process persists after gptme-tauri quits
signals.summary: After quitting gptme-tauri, the gptme-server sidecar process continues running as a zombie orphan. Port 5700 remains occupied, reuse-on-restart logic must silently reattach to the old process, and repeated quit/restart cycles accumulate orphaned processes over time.
aliases: gptme-server zombie process after app quit
tauri app crash leaves server process running
signals.review_reason: Zombie sidecar process causes port 5700 to remain occupied after the app quits, forcing the reuse-on-restart workaround. This is a repeated UX degradation for every Tauri user, and the zombie accumulation over time is a resource leak. Count=2 from two distinct symptom reports (zombie process visible in ps + port-in-use warning on startup), both confirmed by the maintainer.

source_issues.title: bug(tauri): gptme-server sidecar persists after gptme-tauri quits
source_issues.evidence: gptme-server processes visible via ps after quitting gptme-tauri. Multiple child processes orphaned. Port 5700 stays occupied. Repeated quit/restart cycles accumulate zombie processes. 25 comments on the issue. Fix: wire up ServerProcess termination on CloseRequested.

source_issues.title: bug(tauri): server port already in use warning on app startup
source_issues.evidence: Warning about server port already in use on fresh gptme-tauri launch, caused by previous server not being terminated on app close or crash. Classic zombie child process issue.

signals.topic: CI API key invalid/expired blocks all Test workflow runs with 401 errors
signals.summary: The ANTHROPIC_API_KEY GitHub Actions secret is expired or invalid. Every test that makes a real Anthropic API call fails with anthropic.AuthenticationError 401 'invalid x-api-key'. Eight distinct tests are affected including test_vision, test_eval_cli, and test_v2_generate.
signals.review_reason: CI is completely blocked — every API integration test in the Test workflow fails, preventing any merged code from being validated against real API calls. Count=1 but confirmed by CI run log and explicit list of 8 affected test functions.

source_issues.title: fix(ci): ANTHROPIC_API_KEY secret is invalid — all API tests failing with 401
source_issues.evidence: All API tests in the Test workflow failing with 401 authentication_error. Affected tests include test_auto_naming_generates_display_name, test_command_summarize, test_generate_primes, test_url, test_vision, test_eval_cli, test_eval[hello-patch], test_v2_generate. CI run: github.com/gptme/gptme/actions/runs/25110906900

signals.topic: Shell command execution stalls indefinitely in gptme-tauri desktop client
signals.summary: Shell commands executed through gptme-tauri hang with no output, no timeout, and no error. Even simple commands like `ls` never return, forcing users to restart the conversation from CLI. This directly blocks the primary use case of the desktop Tauri app.
signals.review_reason: Core functionality of the Tauri desktop client is broken — users cannot execute any shell commands through the app. Every command stalls silently with no timeout, no error, and no output, completely blocking the main workflow and forcing CLI fallback. Count=1 but confirmed on a simple, universal command (ls).

source_issues.title: bug(tauri): shell command execution stalls (hangs on simple commands like ls)
source_issues.evidence: Shell command execution hangs indefinitely in gptme-tauri. Simple ls command never returned output, requiring conversation restart from CLI. Reported on macOS 15.4.1 with gptme dev build (tauri). May involve tauri frontend-to-server streaming path.

signals.topic: ACP agent UI is incomplete/missing, making ACP feature inaccessible in cloud deployments
signals.summary: ACP agent support backend is merged but the frontend UI for agent selection (sidebar entry, /settings/agent page with dropdown, feature flag enable_acp) is not yet implemented. Feature flag defaults to false. Users cannot switch between OpenHands and ACP agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI) through the UI.
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用。ACP feature的后端已merge但前端完全未实现，feature flag默认为false，cloud用户完全无法使用ACP agent。两条issue count=2，但低于P0的count>=3阈值，降级为P1。严重影响新feature的可用性。

source_issues.title: feat(frontend): ACP agent selection UI — sidebar item, settings pages, dynamic nav
source_issues.evidence: Backend merged (#14004) but frontend implementation is entirely missing. Feature flag enable_acp needs to be added. Agent settings page with type dropdown, API key fields, command/env configuration all need building. Sidebar dynamic gating for ACP mode not implemented.

source_issues.title: feat(acp): minimal generic ACP agent UI (no per-provider scaffolding)
source_issues.evidence: Replaces #14189 with minimal generic ACP UX implementation plan. Specifies settings page with agent type dropdown, command textarea, environment variables textarea, model input. Sidebar gating when ACP active. Per-conversation ACP config snapshot to encrypted JSONB column.

signals.topic: ACP conversation cannot be resumed after sandbox restart in cloud deployments
signals.summary: ACP conversations (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI) are completely lost when cloud sandboxes recycle, because acp_session_id and acp_session_cwd are stored in ephemeral sandbox filesystem and the ACP server's own session files ($HOME) are also wiped. Users lose all conversation history and must start over.
aliases: ACP session not persisted on cloud sandbox recycle
ACP conversations lost after sandbox restart
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断。Cloud部署用户每次sandbox回收后对话历史完全丢失，必须重新开始，且没有workaround。Root cause已明确分析，阻断性明确，符合P0条件。

source_issues.title: ACP: conversations cannot be resumed after sandbox restart (session_id is not persisted)
source_issues.evidence: Root cause clearly identified: acp_session_id and acp_session_cwd are stored in sandbox LocalFileStore (base_state.json) which is wiped on sandbox recycle; ACP server session files live in sandbox $HOME which is also wiped. Proposed fixes include bootstrap-prompt resume and native session/load persist.

signals.topic: Secrets API returns HTTP 200 for update/delete operations on non-existent secrets (silent data corruption)
signals.summary: The update_custom_secret and delete_custom_secret endpoints use 'return HTTPException' instead of 'raise HTTPException', causing a 200 OK response with a serialized HTTPException body instead of a proper 404. Additionally, when the secrets store is empty, the update logic is skipped and a success message is returned even though nothing was written.
aliases: Secret update returns 200 on not found
Secrets endpoint silently fails with 200 OK
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断且数据静默损坏。API返回200表示成功但实际未写入任何数据，客户端误判操作结果，导致用户配置的secrets丢失或管理混乱。代码分析确认两个bug位点，修复明确但当前影响严重。

source_issues.title: Bug: `update_custom_secret` returns 200 when secret doesn't exist (`return` instead of `raise` HTTPException)
source_issues.evidence: Code analysis confirmed two bugs: (1) return HTTPException instead of raise causes 200 response with serialized exception body; (2) empty secrets store bypasses update logic and returns success message. Client believes operation succeeded when it failed. Same pattern exists in delete_custom_secret.

signals.topic: ACP credential file injection not supported for cloud deployments (OAuth-based ACP auth blocked)
signals.summary: ACP agents (Claude Code, Codex) authenticate via local credential files (~/.claude, ~/.codex) from OAuth login. These files live on the user's machine and are inaccessible in cloud deployments where the backend runs on a different host. Previous local-only implementation cannot copy files from the backend filesystem into the sandbox for cloud users.
aliases: ACP OAuth credentials not available in cloud
Credential file injection for ACP agents missing
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用。Cloud用户无法使用OAuth认证方式登录ACP agent，仅能使用API key方式。Root cause清晰，影响明确，cloud部署场景下阻断ACP OAuth认证流程。

source_issues.title: ACP: support credential file injection for cloud deployments
source_issues.evidence: Root cause: credential files live on user's local machine, inaccessible to cloud backend. Previous implementation only worked for self-hosted/local deployments. Proposed: detect FILE: prefix in secrets and write as file in sandbox instead of env var. Two options: paste credential as special secret or dedicated file upload UI.

signals.topic: DeepSeek V4 tool calling fails with 400 Bad Request due to missing reasoning_content field
signals.summary: DeepSeek V4 in thinking mode returns reasoning_content alongside content in assistant responses. When tool calling is triggered, DeepSeek requires reasoning_content to be passed back in message history. OpenHands currently strips or ignores this field, causing 400 invalid_request_error on subsequent requests.
signals.review_reason: 主流程失败。DeepSeek V4 thinking mode用户无法使用tool calling功能，API直接返回400错误。User impact明确，4条评论佐证影响范围。

source_issues.title: [Feature]: Support passing reasoning_content back to API for DeepSeek V4 compatibility
source_issues.evidence: DeepSeek V4 thinking mode returns reasoning_content field. API strictly requires it in message history when tool calling is triggered. Current implementation strips or ignores it to conform to OpenAI API schema, resulting in 400 Bad Request / invalid_request_error on subsequent requests. 4 comments confirming the issue.

signals.topic: AutoPilot requests wrong OAuth credentials (GitHub instead of Gmail) when user attempts Gmail tasks
signals.summary: AutoPilot's prompt injection from prior session memory causes the LLM to emit setup_requirements requesting GitHub credentials instead of Google/Gmail credentials when a user asks to use Gmail. Users must delete all Google integrations and reconnect as a workaround, disrupting their workflow.
aliases: Gmail block requests wrong OAuth scopes
GitHub credentials requested for Gmail tasks
signals.review_reason: This is a user-experienced bug with clear, specific evidence: AutoPilot blocks the Gmail workflow by requesting wrong credentials, forcing users through a destructive workaround (delete all Google integrations + reconnect). The bug is reproducible and has a documented root cause (session memory contamination). While count=1, the evidence is strong and the impact (workflow disruption + credential confusion) is real and not edge-case.

source_issues.title: AutoPilot hallucinates credential prompt for wrong provider - prompts for GitHub credential while it needs Gmail credential for running Gmail block
source_issues.evidence: User asks AutoPilot to write an email via Gmail; AutoPilot emits setup_requirements requesting GitHub credentials (provider:github, scopes:repo) instead of Google. User must delete all Google integrations and reconnect to resolve. Session 73f57993-c371-4619-9b92-bbf3c4027f24, Langfuse trace shows offending tool call. Root cause: memory prompt from prior session contained GitHub credential requests, confusing the LLM.

signals.topic: Navigating to www.platform.agpt.co logs user out and hides agent library
signals.summary: Users who visit the platform at https://www.platform.agpt.co/ are treated as logged-out and see an empty agent library, even when authenticated at https://platform.agpt.co/. The www subdomain is treated as a separate site, breaking the primary user workflow of logging in and accessing saved agents.
aliases: agent library empty on www URL
signals.review_reason: This is a well-documented UX bug with a clear step-by-step reproduction. The primary user workflow (login → access agent library) is broken when users add 'www.' to the URL — a very common user behavior. The workaround is non-obvious and users may not realize why their agents disappeared. Both auth and library access are blocked, making this a clear user pain point even at count=1.

source_issues.title: Adding "www." to the start of the url breaks the platform
source_issues.evidence: Step-by-step reproduction: user visits www.platform.agpt.co, observes they are logged out, re-logs in, visits library, observes zero agents even if they had agents before. The two URLs are treated as separate sites, breaking auth session and library visibility. Also flagged by Ahrefs as 'Duplicate pages without canonical' hurting SEO.

signals.topic: Neovim LSP client crashes when tabby-agent attempts ChatFeature registration, causing autocompletion to stop working
signals.summary: Neovim 0.12.0+ crashes with 'table index is nil' error when tabby-agent tries to register ChatFeature (VSCode-specific functionality), completely breaking LSP-based autocompletion in Neovim/vim-tabby.
aliases: Neovim LSP crash on ChatFeature registration
vim-tabby stops working after tabby-agent update
signals.review_reason: Neovim users experience a crash that blocks the core LSP-based autocompletion workflow. The error is reproducible, affects a specific but real-world client (Neovim + vim-tabby), and renders the extension unusable. Although only 1 issue, the crash is a clear workflow-blocking event with user-confirmed autocompletion failure and a cross-repo confirmed duplicate (vim-tabby#40). Downgraded from P0 because count=1 and single repo — not enough for P0 threshold, but retains P1 due to the severity of the workflow block.

source_issues.title: Neovim LSP Client Crashing on unhandled tabby/chat feature registration
source_issues.evidence: Error message: 'table index is nil' in vim/lsp/client.lua:969; user reports 'vim-tabby / autocompletion stopped working'. Cross-referenced with vim-tabby repo issue #40 confirming same problem. Root cause identified: ChatFeature registration fires for all clients including Neovim, which lacks the required clientInfo handler.

signals.topic: AI thinking 状态下无法点击取消按钮，用户交互被阻断

source_issues.evidence: 标题明确描述 thinking 状态无法停止，截图显示 cancel 按钮相关场景，有环境信息但描述偏简略。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: 赶紧更新新版本吧，deepseek v4报错啊，影响体验啊！
source_issues.evidence: DeepSeek v4 报错，用户明确表示影响体验，但无详细日志和截图，描述较简略。

aliases: 所有工具都没有被正常执行
signals.review_reason: AI 工具执行是 ClawX 核心能力，工具看似正常执行但实际不运行意味着自动化完全失效，属于主流程阻断。用户提供了完整复现步骤（创建文件并验证），证据充分。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: 所有工具都没有被正常执行，显示调用了，但是没有执行
source_issues.evidence: 工具调用显示正常执行（返回成功），但实际 write 方法未运行，无文件生成。步骤清晰：安装后让 AI 写文件，工具被调用但无实际效果。

signals.topic: Stream模式下compression_model触发压缩时崩溃AttributeError
signals.summary: 当ReActAgent配置compression_config且压缩模型复用主模型（stream=True）时，memory压缩触发后_compress_memory_if_needed方法因last_chunk为None访问.metadata属性而崩溃，导致主流程阻断。
aliases: memory compression with streaming model crash
signals.review_reason: 用户主流程（ReActAgent.reply）被明确阻断，有完整复现代码和堆栈证据，且根本原因（流式响应无chunk时last_chunk为None）已在代码中定位，影响核心memory压缩功能，属于高优先级运行时崩溃。

source_issues.title: [Bug]:compression_model 启用 stream=True 时 _compress_memory_if_needed 报 AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'metadata'
source_issues.evidence: 用户提供完整复现代码与堆栈，错误发生在agentscope/agent/_react_agent.py:1112行，当last_chunk为None时访问.metadata导致AttributeError，主流程reply方法被阻断，compression_config使用stream=True的模型压缩功能完全不可用。

signals.topic: DashScopeChatModel对qwen3.6-plus多模态模型路由错误导致图片消息处理失败

source_issues.title: DashScopeChatModel对qwen3.6多模态路由错误
source_issues.evidence: 用户报告qwen3.6-plus不含-vl后缀，被错误路由到纯文本生成API（AioGeneration而非AioMultiModalConversation），文本API无法处理图片消息导致url error，多模态核心功能完全不可用。

signals.topic: ToolGroup.active字段缺少volatile导致多线程动态激活后工具不可用

signals.review_reason: 用户明确报告动态激活工具组后工具不可用，有完整线程时序分析定位根因（字段缺少volatile），属于并发场景下的状态可见性问题，工具组激活核心功能在多线程环境下完全失效，对并发执行场景是明确阻断。count=1故评为P1而非P0。

source_issues.title: [Bug]:工具组动态激活后not available
source_issues.evidence: 用户提供详细线程时序分析：boundedElastic-2写入active=true，boundedElastic-4读取仍为false；根因定位到ToolGroup.active为普通boolean字段无volatile修饰，activeGroups为普通ArrayList，导致多线程写不可见，工具组激活后工具仍报Unauthorized不可用。

signals.topic: HITL（人机交互）暂停机制存在多个关联 bug：stream_events=True 时 TeamRunPausedEvent 不发出；多 HITL 成员并行委托时死锁；acontinue_run 后上下文丢失重复执行
signals.summary: 在 TeamMode.coordinate 下使用 HITL（requires_confirmation=True）工具时，存在三个相互关联的 bug：(1) stream_events=True 导致 TeamRunPausedEvent 从不发出，HITL 核心功能完全失效；(2) Leader 并行委托给多个 HITL 成员时，asyncio.gather 等待所有成员完成导致死锁；(3) 成员级 HITL 暂停解决后调用 acontinue_run，Leader 丢失所有上下文重新规划，导致重复执行和 context 溢出。三个 bug 均使 HITL 工作流无法正常使用。
aliases: acontinue_run loses context after HITL resume
signals.review_reason: 4 个 issue 覆盖同一功能区域（TeamMode.coordinate HITL），均导致 HITL 核心功能不可用或产生死锁/数据丢失：stream_events 模式下暂停事件永不发出（HITL 失效）、并行委托死锁、continue 后上下文丢失导致重复执行、重启后 session 丢失。属于主流程阻断，有 4 个独立 issue 证据且均附有可复现代码，count=4 >= 3，定 P0。

source_issues.title: [Bug] stream_events=True prevents TeamRunPausedEvent from being emitted (HITL broken)
source_issues.evidence: stream_events=True 时 TeamRunPausedEvent 从不发出，requires_confirmation=True 的工具无法触发暂停。关闭 stream_events 则正常。这是 HITL 核心功能失效。

source_issues.title: [Bug] Parallel member delegation with multiple HITL members causes deadlock — TeamRunPausedEvent never emitted
source_issues.evidence: Leader 并行委托给多个 HITL 成员时，asyncio.gather 等待全部完成，HITL 暂停的成员永远无法完成，导致死锁，TeamRunPausedEvent 从不发出。

source_issues.title: [Bug] acontinue_run loses conversation context after member-level HITL resume — Leader re-plans from scratch
source_issues.evidence: 成员级 HITL 暂停解决后 acontinue_run，Leader 创建全新计划并重新委托给所有 Agent，忽略已完成工作，导致重复执行和 context 溢出。

source_issues.title: [Bug] Team.acontinue_run fails to find member agent run after process restart — member session not persisted in coordinate mode
source_issues.evidence: asave_session() 在 agent.team_id 存在时跳过 DB 持久化，acontinue_run 在进程重启后无法从成员自身 session 加载已暂停的运行，HITL workflow 在重启后彻底失败。

signals.topic: BaseDb 子类方法签名与基类不一致，导致 AgentOS API 路由返回 500 错误（SqliteDb/AsyncSqliteDb/RedisDb 的 get_all_memory_topics、get_trace 等方法缺少基类声明的 kwargs）

aliases: BaseDb method signature mismatch breaks API routes

signals.topic: ChromaDb async_insert/async_upsert 实为同步调用，在 asyncio 事件循环线程上执行 Rust 写入，饿死所有协程

signals.topic: Streaming stalls for 50-180 seconds when generating large tool call arguments with high token inputs

signals.topic: MessageStream O(N²) performance degradation during streaming — affects structured output and long responses
signals.summary: MessageStream accumulates streamed text via string concatenation (`+=`) and re-parses the full cumulative JSON buffer on every delta, causing O(N²) complexity. At 4K tokens the slowdown is ~16x; at 10K tokens ~100x. Makes streaming unusable for long structured outputs.
signals.review_reason: Severe performance degradation that makes streaming unusable for long structured outputs. O(N²) complexity causes exponential slowdown with response length. Two independent reports confirm the same root cause. No user workaround exists since accumulation is internal to the SDK.

source_issues.title: perf(MessageStream): O(N²) complexity in text accumulation during structured output streaming
source_issues.evidence: MessageStream accumulates via `accumulated += chunk` (string immutability causes full-copy per concat). For long responses, throughput degrades quadratically. 4K tokens takes ~16x longer than 1K tokens; 10K tokens ~100x slower than optimal. Root cause in MessageStream.ts accumulateContent method.

source_issues.title: O(N²) performance bottleneck in MessageStream during structured output streaming

signals.topic: Subprocess/transport resource leak: BaseExceptionGroup escapes close() on second query, MCP subprocess grandchildren not reaped, transport.close() unguarded
signals.summary: Three related issues converge on resource/signal leak during query lifecycle: (1) BaseExceptionGroup[CancelledError] escapes transport.close() on the second query() call because suppress(Exception) does not catch BaseException subclasses; (2) Query.close() only terminates the CLI process, leaving MCP server subprocess grandchildren reparented to PID 1 and accumulating across repeated calls — causing OOM, file-descriptor exhaustion, CPU burn over hours; (3) transport.close() is the last statement in Query.close() without try/finally, so any earlier cleanup exception skips subprocess termination entirely.
aliases: MCP subprocess leak across query sessions
signals.review_reason: Main flow failure: three distinct issues all causing subprocess/transport resource leaks, with concrete reproduction steps and source-level evidence. The MCP subprocess leak (#889) is a cumulative OOM/fd-exhaustion timebomb for any long-running process; the BaseExceptionGroup crash (#890) blocks repeated query() usage in the same event loop; the unguarded close (#886) silently leaks subprocesses on any error path. All three affect core SDK lifecycle management and are well-evidenced.

source_issues.title: BaseExceptionGroup escapes transport.close() on second query() in the same event loop
source_issues.evidence: Second query() call raises 'BaseExceptionGroup: unhandled errors in a TaskGroup (1 sub-exception) — CancelledError()' from SubprocessCLITransport.close(). Root cause: suppress(Exception) misses BaseExceptionGroup[CancelledError] because CancelledError inherits BaseException (not Exception). Reproducer provided.

source_issues.title: Query.close() does not reap MCP subprocess grandchildren
source_issues.evidence: MCP servers spawned by the CLI reparent to PID 1 after Query.close() and persist until the parent Python process exits. Over a long-running parent (multi-hour pipeline, daemon, test suite) this leaks one MCP server per configured server per dispatch. Verified via pgrep in minimal repro. Manifests as OOM, file-descriptor exhaustion, CPU burn over hours. Affected both macOS and Linux.

source_issues.title: Query.close(): transport.close() not guarded by try/finally — can be skipped if earlier cleanup raises
source_issues.evidence: transport.close() is the last statement in Query.close() with no try/finally. If any preceding cleanup step (transcript-mirror-batcher close, child-task cancel, read-task wait) raises, subprocess and background stderr reader are never cleaned up. Pre-existing issue found during code review of PR #885.

signals.topic: MCP server stdio tools not registered on Windows — agent sees server instructions but all tools return 'No such tool available'
signals.summary: On Windows 11 + Python 3.14, when MCP servers are configured via stdio transport in `mcp_servers={}`, the server's instructions are injected into the agent's context but none of its tools are callable. Every tool call returns 'No such tool available'. The same code worked on 2026-04-30 morning and broke that evening with no code changes. This is 100% reproducible and blocks all agentic workflows relying on stdio MCP servers on Windows.
aliases: MCP stdio tools not callable on Windows
MCP server tools invisible to agent on Windows
signals.review_reason: Core workflow blocker: MCP server configuration is a primary SDK use case, and the complete failure to expose callable tools means agentic workflows dependent on stdio MCP servers are fully blocked on Windows. Evidence is concrete: reproducible 100% failure rate, clear agent diagnostic, verified MCP server works standalone, multiple attempted fixes documented.

source_issues.title: MCP server tools fail to register on Windows: server config visible to agent but tools return "No such tool available"
source_issues.evidence: 100% reproducible across ~6 attempts on Windows 11 + Python 3.14. Agent diagnostic confirms: 'Supabase MCP server's guidelines are visible... but none of its callable tools are reachable — every attempt returns No such tool available.' MCP server verified working standalone via direct npx. All attempted workarounds (downgrade SDK, wildcard allowed_tools, full env passthrough, move to C:\, restart) failed. Blocks all stdio-MCP-based agentic workflows on this environment.

signals.topic: List-form system_prompt crashes SubprocessCLITransport._build_command with AttributeError — blocks prompt caching use case and burns API cost
signals.summary: SubprocessCLITransport._build_command raises AttributeError ('list' object has no attribute 'get') when system_prompt is passed as a list of content blocks, which is a valid Anthropic Messages API format and is required for layer-independent prompt caching with cache_control. The SDK does not validate this shape at ClaudeAgentOptions construction time, so the crash is delayed to command-build time. Users burned real money ($0.46 reported) before encountering the crash. The only workaround flattens the list to a string, sacrificing cache efficiency.
aliases: list-form system prompt not supported by SDK transport
signals.review_reason: Functional failure: the SDK rejects a valid Anthropic API format for system_prompt, causing an immediate AttributeError crash before any model call. Prompt caching (a billed feature) is blocked — the workaround explicitly sacrifices cache efficiency. Real financial cost ($0.46) burned before crash is documented. This is not a theoretical limitation; it actively breaks a documented Anthropic API usage pattern.

source_issues.title: subprocess CLI rejects list-form system_prompt (Anthropic API supports it)
source_issues.evidence: AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get' at subprocess_cli.py:215 in _build_command. Real cost burned before crash: $0.46. Root cause: SDK only accepts str/None/SystemPromptFile/SystemPromptPreset for system_prompt, but Anthropic Messages API accepts string | content_block[] and prompt caching documentation recommends list form with cache_control on trailing block. Workaround of concatenating to string regresses cache efficiency (loses layer-independent caching benefit). Reproducer provided with claude-agent-sdk 0.1.66, bundled CLI 2.1.119.

signals.topic: Windows command line overflow when system_prompt exceeds 32,767 chars — SDK misattributes FileNotFoundError(WinError 206) to missing binary
signals.summary: On Windows, passing a large system_prompt (e.g., 48K chars from RAG-injected content) causes Python's subprocess.CreateProcess to raise FileNotFoundError with WinError 206 'filename or extension too long'. The SDK's error handler catches this as FileNotFoundError and re-raises it as CLINotFoundError('Claude Code not found'), completely misattributing the cause. The workaround (--system-prompt-file flag) exists in the CLI but is not used by the SDK as a fallback. Users lose hours investigating a 'missing binary' that isn't missing.
aliases: Windows CreateProcess 32,767 char limit hits system_prompt
WinError 206 misdiagnosed as missing CLI binary
signals.review_reason: Main flow failure on Windows: any production workflow that injects RAG/retrieved context into system_prompt will hit this on first non-trivial query. The error message is actively misleading (points to missing binary when the issue is command-line length), causing significant diagnostic time loss. The fix is mechanical — the SDK already has a temp-file fallback pattern for --agents that can be mirrored for --system-prompt.

source_issues.title: Windows: SDK should fall back to --system-prompt-file when cmdline overflows (follow-up to #501)
source_issues.evidence: FileNotFoundError WinError 206 on system_prompt ~48,755 chars. SDK raises CLINotFoundError('Claude Code not found at: ...') — completely wrong error message. User lost ~90 minutes investigating a binary that existed and ran fine standalone. RAG/knowledge-grounded bots on Windows are the natural use case for large system_prompt — they hit this on first non-trivial query. The CLI flag --system-prompt-file exists but SDK does not use it as fallback. Reproducer confirmed on Windows 11, Python 3.14.3, SDK 0.1.x.

signals.topic: TaskNotificationMessage delivered prematurely while subagent is still executing — causes cascading downstream dispatch errors
signals.summary: When an orchestrator dispatches multiple subagents in parallel via the Task tool, the SDK sometimes delivers TaskNotificationMessage (<task-notification> SystemMessage) to the orchestrator while the referenced subagent is still actively executing tool calls. The notification fires before the subagent's ResultMessage, sometimes 76–850 seconds early. The orchestrator acts on the premature completion signal, dispatching downstream agents against files that haven't been written yet, causing cascading failures, wasted compute, and duplicate work. Non-deterministic (1 of 2 identical runs triggered the issue).
aliases: Task tool notification fires before subagent completion
Premature task completion signal corrupts orchestrator workflow
signals.review_reason: Orchestration workflow corruption: premature task-completion signals cause cascading downstream dispatch errors with measurable cost impact ($21.51 wasted vs $22.33 for correct run) and wasted wall time. The orchestrator's event-driven pattern is fundamentally broken when completion signals fire mid-execution. Non-deterministic nature makes this especially dangerous as it silently corrupts results in production.

source_issues.title: [Bug] TaskNotificationMessage fires while subagent is still running (premature, not cross-turn leak)
source_issues.evidence: Non-deterministic (1/2 runs). In affected run: all 5 subagents received premature <task-notification> while still mid-execution. Orchestrator acted on notifications, dispatched reviewers against non-existent files, wasted ~8 min re-dispatching researchers, then received actual TASK_DONE ~17 minutes later. Measurable cost impact: 32 min/$21.51 (broken) vs 51 min/$22.33 (correct baseline). Orchestrator prompt uses event-driven pattern that depends on accurate completion signals. Log evidence with exact timestamps and tool counts provided.

signals.topic: Silent process exit (code 1) in v0.2.121 when calling query() in production server context
signals.summary: SDK v0.2.121 silently crashes the Node.js process with exit code 1 when query() is called in a production server context. No exception is thrown, no stack trace is logged, and uncaughtException/unhandledRejection handlers do not fire. Process terminates at the SDK boundary with zero diagnostic output, making the SDK completely unusable in production at v0.2.121. Downgrading to v0.2.70 is the only workaround.
signals.review_reason: Critical production blocker: the entire Node.js process terminates silently without any error signal when query() is invoked in a real server environment at v0.2.121. No exception, no diagnostic, no recovery. Users must downgrade to an older version to regain functionality. This is a complete main-flow failure for all production deployments at the current version.

source_issues.title: Silent process exit (code 1) when calling query() from SDK v0.2.121
source_issues.evidence: Process silently exits with code 1 after calling query(). No exception thrown, no stack trace, uncaughtException and unhandledRejection handlers do not fire. Crash is deterministic in production server context, reproducible across Windows/macOS/Linux. Workaround: downgrade to v0.2.70. 0 comments, 0 replies — issue has not been addressed.

signals.topic: Cache creation token overcounting: SDK charges 1.25x write cost for content already in cache read prefix
signals.summary: On every turn, the SDK reports ~65K cache_creation_input_tokens even for null-content exchanges (e.g., 'ok thanks'). cache_read works correctly, proving the prefix is cached, yet the SDK still pays the 1.25x cache-write rate for ~65K of content per turn instead of the 0.1x read rate. This creates a persistent ~$0.50–0.65/turn cost floor on trivial exchanges, estimated at ~$5K/month fleet-wide for 35 agents at 50 turns/day.
aliases: cache_read works but cache_create still charged
signals.review_reason: Direct financial loss: the SDK charges the expensive cache-write rate (1.25x) for content that is provably already cached (cache_read working correctly), when it should charge the cheap cache-read rate (0.1x). Every turn, even trivial exchanges, incurs a $0.50–0.65 cost floor from this phantom write. Multiplied across fleet agents, this is a significant and systematic cost leak with no user-visible way to suppress it.

source_issues.title: cache issues in sdk
source_issues.evidence: Detailed telemetry: Turn 1 cache_create=65,136 / cache_read=180,339 at $0.51 cost; Turn 2 'ok thanks' (3 tokens) cache_create=65,488 / cache_read=305,175 at $0.58 cost; Turn 3 cache_create=65,627 / cache_read=430,363 at $0.64 cost. ~zero new content but cache_create stays at ~65K floor. FUTURES_MANAGER agent: ~162K floor per turn. The content IS being read from cache correctly but the SDK still pays to write ~65K fresh. Author estimates ~$175/day fleet-wide, ~$5K/month attributable to this floor.

signals.topic: SDK unconditionally forwards Anthropic-only beta headers to Vertex AI, causing 100% request failure with no opt-out mechanism
signals.summary: The SDK hardcodes beta tokens ('effort-2025-11-24', 'tool-search-tool-2025-10-19', 'web-search-2025-03-05') in the bundled CLI and forwards them unconditionally in the anthropic-beta header. Vertex AI rejects these with HTTP 400. There is no documented or public way to disable these beta headers when targeting Vertex AI, forcing users to run an in-house proxy to strip them.
signals.review_reason: Full workflow blockage for Vertex AI users: every single API request fails with HTTP 400 because the SDK forwards beta headers that Vertex has never accepted. There is no documented opt-out, so the only path to Vertex compatibility is running a custom proxy — an unreasonable burden for production deployments. This is a complete functional failure for a specific provider path.

source_issues.title: Vertex AI 400: SDK forwards `effort-2025-11-24`, `tool-search-tool-2025-10-19`, `web-search-2025-03-05` betas that Vertex doesn't accept
source_issues.evidence: 100% failure rate on Vertex-backed chat traffic. Error: 'Unexpected value(s) effort-2025-11-24, tool-search-tool-2025-10-19, web-search-2025-03-05 for the anthropic-beta header.' The tokens are hardcoded in the bundled CLI binary (verified via strings). The SDK's own bundled text acknowledges these betas should be removed for newer model lineups but still attaches them unconditionally. No public API to opt out without monkey-patching the bundled CLI.

signals.topic: API 400 errors return empty response body, blocking user workflow with no retry or diagnostic path
signals.summary: When calling the SDK with a custom API endpoint (non-Anthropic-direct), the API returns HTTP 400 with no response body. The error message is generic and provides zero diagnostic context (no shape problem detected, 0 tool calls/results/history reported). canRetry is set to false, preventing automatic retry. Error messages lack connection name and model details, making root-cause diagnosis impossible.
signals.review_reason: Recurrent workflow blockage (13 errors in 1.5 hours) with zero diagnostic information. Users cannot distinguish between auth failures, rate-limit rejections, and format errors because the SDK swallows the 400 response body. The canRetry=false flag prevents any recovery attempt. This leaves users completely blind when their custom endpoint rejects requests.

source_issues.title: 400 status code (no body)
source_issues.evidence: 13 errors over ~1.5 hours, 8 of which were 400 (no body) in 4 independent events. Error message: '400 status code (no body). Endpoint rejected the request with no body (no obvious shape problem). Last request: 0 tool call(s), 0 tool result(s), 0 history entries. Try a different endpoint.' canRetry: false. No response body provided. Environment: custom connection pi-api-key-4, model claude-opus-4-7. User cannot determine if issue is auth, rate-limit, or format.

signals.topic: outputFormat reports subtype 'success' but structured_output is undefined for complex schemas, misleading callers
signals.summary: When using outputFormat with complex (nested) JSON schemas, the SDK returns subtype='success' even though structured_output is undefined (absent from the result). The model correctly produces JSON in the result text, but the SDK fails to extract or validate it. Callers relying on subtype cannot distinguish success from silently missing output, and cannot detect when to fall back to manual JSON parsing.
signals.review_reason: Key feature failure: structured output with complex schemas is advertised as working ('you still get validated JSON matching your schema at the end' per docs) but silently returns subtype='success' with no structured_output for any non-trivial schema. Users who check subtype alone cannot detect this failure, leaving them with undefined output and no signal to retry or parse result text manually. This defeats the purpose of structured output for real-world schema complexity.

source_issues.title: outputFormat returns subtype 'success' when structured_output is absent — should return error_max_structured_output_retries
source_issues.evidence: Nested schemas (3+ levels, additionalProperties:false on every object) consistently return subtype:'success' with structured_output:undefined. Simple 2-field schemas work correctly. Model produces correct JSON in result text (confirmed), proving the API supports the schema — the SDK extraction/validation layer fails. 6 comments, actively being worked. Testing matrix shows all nested/deep/$ref schemas fail with no structured_output.

signals.topic: Internal error 'directory mismatch' causes complete workflow failure on every run
signals.summary: Action logs 'directory mismatch' internal error before any tool dispatch and returns exit 1, failing every run. Users report disabling the action entirely and routing to local cursor-agent dispatch as workaround. Regression identified within narrow window on 2026-04-26.
signals.review_reason: Issue #1266 is a direct 'fails on every run' workflow blocker with confirmed regression on 2026-04-26. Issue #1272 shows the same 'directory mismatch' internal error as a secondary symptom, indicating the same root cause affecting multiple repos. The user's only workaround is to disable the action entirely, constituting a full main-flow failure.

source_issues.title: Internal error: directory mismatch for '.../claude-code-action/<ref>/tsconfig.json', fd 4 — fails on every run
source_issues.evidence: Every run logs 'directory mismatch' error before tool dispatch, returns exit 1. User disabled workflow entirely and routed to local cursor-agent dispatch as workaround. Regression confirmed within narrow window on 2026-04-26 ~22:50 UTC.

source_issues.title: [BUG] 'Claude Code is not installed on this repository' for previously-working github actions across multiple repos on 2026-04-28
source_issues.evidence: Previously-working action across multiple repos started failing with 'Claude Code is not installed' error AND 'directory mismatch' internal error on 2026-04-28. Restored only by manually reinstalling the Claude App on the org. Audit log shows NO uninstall event.

signals.topic: Action fails on PRs with newly added files — git hash-object called before PR checkout
signals.summary: Action attempts to compute git SHA hashes for all changed files before checking out the PR branch, causing git hash-object to fail for files marked 'ADDED' (which don't exist in base). Users must use CLI locally as the only workaround.
aliases: git hash-object fails for ADDED files
PR with new files fails before checkout
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow blocker: the action fails on ANY PR that introduces new files, which is one of the most common real-world PR patterns. The failure occurs before the PR is even checked out, meaning no workflow configuration can work around it. The only workaround is using the CLI locally instead of the action. High impact despite count=1 because the failure mode is deterministic and affects a fundamental use case.

source_issues.title: Action fails on PRs with newly added files - git hash-object called before PR checkout
source_issues.evidence: Action calls fetchGitHubData() which runs git hash-object on each changed file BEFORE checking out PR branch. Files marked 'ADDED' don't exist in current checkout (base branch), causing 'fatal: could not open file for reading: No such file or directory'. Error confirmed at src/github/data/fetcher.ts:354. No workaround available from workflow config.

signals.topic: anthropic_api_key gives misleading 'Credit balance is too low' error when Claude Code subscription required
signals.summary: Setting up action with a valid anthropic_api_key (with credits on platform.claude.com) fails instantly with misleading 'Credit balance is too low' error. The real issue is that Claude Code requires a subscription or OAuth token, not just API credits. Documentation does not clarify this.
aliases: API key vs OAuth token confusion
signals.review_reason: This is a setup-blocking issue: users with valid API credentials and credits cannot get the action running because the error message misleads them into thinking they need more credits, when the actual root cause is a credential type mismatch. The README is documented as misleading, and 6 comments indicate widespread confusion. The billing separation between claude.ai and platform.claude.com is nowhere documented. This prevents initial setup success for a clearly-identified user segment.

source_issues.title: anthropic_api_key insufficient - misleading 'Credit balance is too low' error when Claude Code subscription required
source_issues.evidence: Action fails instantly (180ms, $0 cost) with 'Credit balance is too low' when using anthropic_api_key without a linked Claude Code subscription. The error is completely misleading — the user had $30 credits on platform.claude.com. README implies anthropic_api_key is sufficient, but claude_code_oauth_token is the actual correct credential for most users. 6 comments indicate ongoing confusion.

signals.topic: False positive multi-operation detection blocks valid bash commands (awk, python3 -c) causing job cancellation
signals.summary: The multi-operation safety detector incorrectly blocks several valid bash patterns (awk with && in pattern, python3 -c inline). Each false positive requires approval and accumulates toward the 80-turn limit, eventually causing the job to be cancelled with 'Error: The operation was canceled.'
signals.review_reason: False positive permission blocks are a direct experience degradation — they consume turn budget and can lead to job cancellation, which is a failure of the main review task. This is a repeatable failure pattern on a standard CLI tool (awk) and a common one-liner pattern (python3 -c). The workaround requires users to preemptively instruct Claude about command syntax, which is not a normal user expectation.

source_issues.title: False positive multi-operation detection blocks valid bash commands (awk, python3 -c, Windows path pattern)
source_issues.evidence: Claude used valid awk command 'awk NR>=270 && NR<=310 file.js' which was blocked because && inside the awk pattern was misidentified as command chaining. Similarly python3 -c inline was blocked. False positives accumulate toward 80-turn limit and cause 'Error: The operation was canceled.' Users must manually instruct Claude to use alternative commands as a workaround.

signals.topic: .claude-pr/ snapshot directory accidentally committed to user PR branch by bot fix-up commits
signals.summary: The .claude-pr/ directory created by restoreConfigFromBase is unintentionally committed to the user's PR branch whenever the bot makes a fix-up commit. The bot's reply comment doesn't acknowledge this, creating stealth commits that pollute the PR history with unrelated files.
signals.review_reason: This causes real PR pollution: unrelated commits appear in the user's branch history without any notification from the bot. The bot's own comment is silent about the extra commit, leaving users to discover it only on git log review. The fix is straightforward (add to .git/info/exclude), but users have no way to detect or prevent this from the workflow side. This degrades trust in the bot's commit hygiene.

source_issues.title: restoreConfigFromBase snapshot at '.claude-pr/' gets committed to PR branch when bot pushes a fix
source_issues.evidence: Real-world incidents: (1) chore commit adding .claude-pr/ (~100 files) on a PR about hardware OEM project structure — completely unrelated. (2) second chore commit re-syncing .claude-pr/ on a different PR. In both cases the bot's reply summarized only the requested change, so maintainers only noticed the extra commit on review. No signal is given to users that .claude-pr/ was committed.

signals.topic: Rate limiting (429) blocks security review runs with no throttling option
signals.summary: 用户在使用安全审查工具时频繁遭遇 429 rate limit 错误，因工具未提供请求节流机制导致主流程反复阻断。
signals.review_reason: 虽然是单条 issue，但 429 错误直接阻断用户执行安全审查的核心工作流，用户明确表示'getting rate limited all the time'，属于主流程反复失败，具有明确的用户影响证据（主流程阻断 + 计费/配额异常），符合痛点定义中的'主流程失败/阻断'。因 count=1，不满足 P0 的高频要求（count>=3），但影响明确，故标记为 P1。

source_issues.title: I'm getting rate limited all the time
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly reports being rate limited 'all the time' during security review runs, receiving 429 errors ('This request would exceed your organization's rate limit of 10,000 input tokens per minute'), with no workaround available and explicitly requests throttling mechanism.

aliases: ultrareview skill crash consumes free credits

source_issues.evidence: Ran /ultrareview on a PR; CLI reported 'Free ultrareview 2 of 3'; after ~5-10 min received error 'Review crashed before producing findings'. Free credit consumed despite zero output. User requests credit refund.

signals.topic: Desktop app silently doubles cache_creation token consumption compared to VS Code extension — material cost increase

aliases: cache_creation token doubling desktop app migration
system prompt inflation desktop app vs extension
