Cache_creation per turn doubled and daily cost rose 2.45x — direct monetary impact for a Max plan subscriber. The silence (no disclosure, no control) makes it functionally indistinguishable from a cost regression. Clear user-visible cost impact, not merely a performance concern.

source_issues.title: Cache_creation tokens per turn doubled (2.18x) after migrating from VS Code extension to desktop app — Opus 4.7 / Max plan

signals.topic: SSH session RPC stream closes after exactly 14s — remote development on macOS fully blocked
signals.summary: On macOS Desktop, SSH sessions establish successfully but the RPC stream closes at exactly 14 seconds on every connection. ccd-cli is never spawned; no prompts can be sent. Full reinstalls, MTU adjustments, and token refreshes do not resolve it.
aliases: SSH session disconnects unilaterally after 14 seconds
signals.review_reason: Remote development via SSH on macOS is completely blocked — the session connects but no prompt can ever be sent because the RPC stream drops at exactly 14s before ccd-cli spawns. Has clear reproduction logs with exact timestamps. Main flow for SSH remote users is fully broken.

source_issues.title: SSH session: RPC stream closes after 14s, ccd-cli never spawned, Mac client disconnects unilaterally
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible with exact timestamps: stream opened at 00:05:09, closed at 00:05:23 (14s). Server logs confirm only ping requests received, no session.start RPC ever sent. signals.topic: Windows REPL silently exits during long-running agents with dense Bash subprocess chains — session work lost

aliases: Windows REPL silent crash long-running agent

source_issues.evidence: Reproduced 3 times in one morning: long-running agents (10-30 min), 50+ Bash tool uses with chained subprocesses, REPL vanishes silently leaving stranded characters at bare PS prompt. Session work lost. User refers to similar silent failure pattern in #55033 and #54426 in the same v2.1.121 timeframe.

signals.topic: Windows: mkdir EEXIST in SessionStart hook and Bash tool session-env bootstrap — Bash tool fully blocked

aliases: Windows mkdir EEXIST blocks Bash tool
EEXIST mkdir Windows session-env Bash failure

skills notebook prerequisites missing github step

Count=1 and single-repo, so P0 thresholds are not met; however the experience is unambiguously broken for every new learner (structural issue, not edge case), warranting P1.

source_issues.title: [BUG] intro to skills should point at github repo as install prereq
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly describes being blocked mid-recipe: tried to follow instructions but had no idea where '/path/to/claude-cookbooks/skills' comes from. 'be frustrated' is the direct user impact statement.

signals.topic: Telegram plugin MCP polling silently stalls — inbound messages stop with no error
signals.summary: Telegram plugin's MCP polling loop exits prematurely when bot.start() resolves without an explicit shutdown signal, causing the bot to appear healthy (process alive, outbound calls work) while inbound messages stop arriving entirely. Only remedy is full process restart.
signals.review_reason: Multiple confirmed occurrences in production (7 times in 10 days for polling stall alone). All forms result in silent message loss — users receive no response and the bot appears functional from outside. Requires manual process restart to recover. #1620 additionally causes file corruption and session deadlock. This is a main-flow silent failure that is hard to diagnose externally.

source_issues.title: fix(telegram): retry polling on silent bot.start() resolution
source_issues.evidence: Observed 7 times across 10 days in field use. MCP looks healthy from outside, but inbound Telegram messages stop arriving in Claude Code. No errors logged. Only resolution is restarting Claude Code.

source_issues.title: Telegram bridge MCP transport drops during long-running tool calls
source_issues.evidence: MCP connection goes silent during tool calls exceeding ~60 seconds. Transport times out. User has to manually restart Claude. No automatic reconnection.

source_issues.title: Plugin loaded via --plugin-dir connects but doesn't inject channel messages
source_issues.evidence: When plugin is scope-loaded via --plugin-dir, MCP connects but channel-message injection silently fails. Inbound DMs reach bun but never inject into the Claude session. No reply arrives in Telegram.

source_issues.title: [telegram] local Bot API mode (TELEGRAM_API_ROOT) saves 404 JSON as .jpg, deadlocks session
source_issues.evidence: Plugin writes 404 JSON response as .jpg file. Model reads corrupted file, API returns 400. Session deadlocks on retry loop until user manually exits. Lost ~10 minutes.

signals.topic: iMessage chat_messages auto-embeds unsupported images, causing HTTP 400 retry loop that deadlocks the agent
signals.summary: The iMessage MCP chat_messages tool automatically attempts to embed image attachments as multimodal content. When the image format is unsupported (e.g., HEIC from iPhone) or causes HTTP 400, the tool retries indefinitely without surfacing an error, freezing the agent for minutes until external restart.
aliases: iMessage MCP image 400 loop agent deadlock
iMessage attachment embed HTTP 400 infinite retry
signals.review_reason: Confirmed agent deadlock for 12 minutes in production. Root cause verified via chat.db post-mortem. HEIC is the default iPhone photo format since 2017, making this a high-probability recurring issue for any iPhone-heavy deployment. The retry loop without error surfacing is a particularly insidious failure shape — the agent appears 'busy' rather than erroring, making diagnosis difficult without external observation.

source_issues.title: chat_messages should support text-only mode (or fail-fast on attachment fetch) to bypass auto-embedded image fetches that 400-and-loop
source_issues.evidence: Verified incident: 12 minutes of agent stuck state (2026-04-26 17:38-17:50 BST) on a single HEIC attachment. Agent appeared 'busy' (in-flight tool call with no progress). Recovery required external process restart. Root cause confirmed: iPhone HEIC (image/heic) is not supported by Anthropic API, plugin passed bytes through without conversion, producing 400 'Could not process image'. Agent was unresponsive to watcher nudges.

source_issues.title: imessage: HEIC attachments from iPhone exceed Read tool's 256KB limit; consider auto-converting to JPEG
source_issues.evidence: iPhone HEIC attachments (typically 1-3 MB) exceed Claude Code's Read tool 256KB limit. Read fails with 'File content (1.3MB) exceeds maximum allowed size (256KB)'. Plugin emits image_path pointing at HEIC, assistant tries Read, fails. Workaround requires manual sips conversion.

signals.topic: Plugin visible on marketplace website but not discoverable in Claude Code desktop tool
signals.summary: Plugins that have Published status on the Claude plugin marketplace website are not appearing in the Claude Code desktop application plugin discovery UI, preventing users from installing and enabling them through the desktop experience. The website and desktop tool appear to use different indexes or caches.
aliases: Plugin not showing in Claude Code desktop tool
Marketplace plugin not discoverable in desktop UI
Plugin discovery index mismatch website vs desktop
signals.review_reason: Two independent plugin maintainers have confirmed the same discovery gap. When a plugin has Published status on the web marketplace but is not visible in the desktop tool, users cannot find and install it through the intended discovery flow. This breaks plugin discoverability for multiple plugins and suggests a systematic index synchronization issue.

source_issues.title: MercadoPago plugin is not appearing at Claude Code
source_issues.evidence: User has Published status for Mercado Pago plugin on the marketplace website, but the plugin is not visible in Claude Code's plugin discovery UI. Screenshot shows the plugin appears in the web marketplace but not in the desktop tool.

source_issues.title: Cosmos DB plugin not discoverable in desktop tool
source_issues.evidence: Cosmos DB plugin maintainer confirms plugin is discoverable on the marketplace website but not in the Claude desktop/tool experience. User asks whether desktop discovery uses a different index or cache, and whether the pinned marketplace SHA needs refreshing.

signals.topic: skill-creator run_loop completely unusable on Windows — two sequential crashes prevent any results
signals.summary: The skill-creator's description-optimization loop fails for every Windows user. First, select.select() on pipe file descriptors throws WinError 10038 (Windows only supports select on sockets). Second, Path.write_text() with platform default encoding (cp1252) crashes on the ✗ character used in HTML reports.
aliases: skill-creator cp1252 encoding crash on Windows
signals.review_reason: Two sequential bugs ensure the entire skill-optimization workflow fails for all Windows users before producing any results. Bug 1 causes 100% query failure (silent — returns False, not an error). Bug 2 crashes the script before results can be saved. Combined with the large Windows user base (~1/3 of devs), this makes the skill-creator plugin entirely non-functional for a significant population.

source_issues.title: skill-creator: run_loop fails on Windows (select.select on pipes + cp1252 encoding)
source_issues.evidence: Bug 1: select.select() only works on sockets on Windows — throws WinError 10038 on every subprocess invocation, causing 100% query failure (every query returns False, counted as 'did not trigger'). Bug 2: Path.write_text() uses cp1252 encoding on Windows, crashes on ✗ character with UnicodeEncodeError before any results are saved. Together, the plugin is completely unusable for Windows users. Author estimates roughly a third of devs are on Windows.

signals.topic: M365 connector authorization fails with vague error, blocking enterprise Microsoft integration setup
signals.summary: The M365 connector fails authorization with a generic error message 'Authorization with the MCP server failed. You can check your credentials and permissions' even after granting all required Azure AD permissions, including Global Administrator. The error is inconsistent — works for some users, fails for others — and provides no actionable debug path.
aliases: Microsoft 365 connector OAuth admin consent failure
signals.review_reason: M365 connector is a core enterprise integration. Authorization failure blocks the entire setup flow with a vague error that provides no debug path. The inconsistency (works for some, fails for others) combined with the opaque error reference suggests a deeper auth/tenant issue that enterprise IT admins cannot self-diagnose.

source_issues.title: [BUG] M365 Connector: Authorization with the MCP server failed. You can check your credentials and permissions. ofid_e4f0d80ee795b604
source_issues.evidence: User attempted full Microsoft 365 integration setup following official documentation, granted all permissions including Global Administrator. Authorization still fails with opaque error and reference ID. Inconsistency confirmed: the same setup worked for one user but failed for another even with elevated permissions. No debug path available.

signals.topic: Windows 环境下 skill-creator 脚本无法运行，核心优化器流程完全阻断
signals.summary: skill-creator 的三个 Windows 兼容性问题导致脚本完全无法在原生 Windows 上运行：(1) subprocess.Popen 无法找到 .cmd 文件；(2) Unicode 字符写入文件报编码错误；(3) select.select() 在 Windows 上不支持管道 fd，导致所有查询立即报错 [WinError 10038]，优化器核心流程无法执行。
signals.review_reason: Issue 3 明确标注为 BLOCKING，select.select() 在 Windows 管道上直接抛出 [WinError 10038] 导致 run_eval/run_loop 全部查询失败，优化器核心流程完全无法执行，用户研究验证端到端失败。三个问题叠加导致原生 Windows 用户完全无法使用 skill-creator，这是明确的主流程阻断。

source_issues.title: Windows compatibility: skill-creator scripts fail (subprocess PATHEXT, cp1252 encoding, select on pipes)
source_issues.evidence: Issue 3 (BLOCKING): select.select() raises [WinError 10038] on Windows, blocking ALL queries in run_eval/run_loop/improve_description — 'Warning: query failed: [WinError 10038] An operation was attempted on something that is not a socket'. Verified end-to-end on native Windows Python 3.14.

signals.topic: docx skill 生成的 Word 文件无法被 Microsoft Word 正常打开
signals.summary: docx skill 在生成 .docx 文件时产生 Microsoft Word 标记为「发现无法读取的内容」的错误，导致用户无法使用生成的文档。根因包括：XML text 节点内含换行符、header/footer r:id 硬编码错误、numbering.xml 缺少必需元素。
signals.review_reason: docx skill 生成的文件无法被 Microsoft Word 正常打开，用户得到损坏的文档无法使用，这是明确的产出物不可用（关键功能不可用）。用户报告在 Ubuntu 26.04 上稳定复现，三处 XML 编辑根因均已定位，符合主流程阻断级别的用户痛点。

source_issues.title: docx skill no longer works on Ubuntu 26.04
source_issues.evidence: Skill 生成 .docx 文件后 Microsoft Word 打开时报 'Word found unreadable content' 并提供恢复，导致用户文档损坏无法使用。问题复现于 Ubuntu 26.04，三个 XML 编辑根因均已提供修复方案。

signals.topic: PDF skill 对无结构表（定位排版表）的多页提取失败且大文档 OOM
signals.summary: PDF skill 推荐的方法对「假表格」（无 PDF 表格结构，仅靠 x/y 坐标定位的文本）完全无效；pdftotext -layout 在多页时因每页字符宽度重算导致列偏移，解析器在续页失败；大文档（3000+ 页）因 pdfplumber 缓存机制导致内存线性增长直至 OOM 被 kill。
aliases: PDF 多页表格提取列偏移
signals.review_reason: PDF 表提取是 PDF skill 的核心功能之一，对无结构表完全失效且多页场景下有列偏移 bug，同时大文档有 OOM 风险（3000+ 页生产环境验证）。用户在生成环境中实际遇到这些失败，skill.md 缺少相关警示导致用户反复踩坑，符合体验显著下降 + 关键功能部分不可用的痛点标准。

source_issues.title: pdf skill: `pdftotext -layout` column-drift on multi-page positional "tables"
source_issues.evidence: pdftotext -layout 对多页文档每页重新缩放字符列宽，导致续页列位置漂移，解析器在 continuation pages 失效；大文档（~3000页 / 5500页总长）因 pdfplumber 缓存 per-page parse state 且未 flush cache 导致内存线性增长，在 ~3000 页处被 OOM kill。提供了真实生产环境的复现链接。

signals.topic: Windows 严重磁盘泄漏：MCP 子进程 / LLM 日志 / 临时文件三重泄漏，7 个月积累约 350GB
signals.summary: Windows 环境下 MCP 子进程退出后从不清理、LLM 请求日志以二次方速度增长（无轮转）、工具执行的临时文件从不清理，三者叠加造成灾难性磁盘空间损耗。
aliases: temp files never cleaned up Windows
signals.review_reason: 明确的主流程阻断：Windows 用户磁盘空间被逐步耗尽，三个独立泄漏机制均有具体数量估算，5-7 个月内造成 350GB 累积损耗，属于严重资源泄漏。

source_issues.title: [Windows] Goose never cleans up after itself — ~350GB disk leak over 7 months
source_issues.evidence: 报告 7 个月内积累约 350GB：MCP 子进程从不终止，重启后累积 41 个进程占 ~900MB RAM；llm_request.*.jsonl 以二次方增长 5 个月约 100-150GB；临时文件约 2100 个目录估计 50-100GB。无任何清理机制。

signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：新用户首次配置时配置向导直接报错退出，导致 Goose 完全不可用，属于关键的初始化流程失败。

source_issues.title: Configuration wizard error: Configuration value not found

source_issues.title: Gemini OAuth flow fails for Gemini Pro/Advanced accounts (400 Bad Request: INVALID_ARGUMENT)

signals.topic: FlowLogger 导致 Stagehand 在 Cloudflare Workers 上启动时立即崩溃
signals.summary: v3.2.0+ 引入的 FlowLogger 在 init 时调用 AsyncLocalStorage.enterWith()，而 Cloudflare Workers 不支持该 API，导致 stagehand.init() 立即抛出 'enterWith() is not implemented' 错误，完全阻断在 Workers 环境下的使用。
aliases: AsyncLocalStorage.enterWith not supported on CF Workers
signals.review_reason: 明确的运行时崩溃：v3.2.0+ 引入 FlowLogger 后，在 Cloudflare Workers 环境下 stagehand.init() 立即失败，完全阻断主流程。根因清晰（enterWith() 在 CF Workers 中未实现），影响所有在该环境下使用 v3.2.0+ 的用户。虽然 count=1 不满足 P0 高频要求，但 startup_crash 类别在优先级判断时应高于 count 权重，因此标记为 P1 而非 P2。

source_issues.title: FlowLogger breaks on Cloudflare Workers: enterWith() is not supported
source_issues.evidence: 用户在 Cloudflare Workers (Durable Objects) 环境下运行 stagehand.init() 时，v3.2.0+ 版本直接抛出 'asyncLocalStorage.enterWith() is not implemented' 错误，发生在任何浏览器交互之前，属于启动时阻断性崩溃。

signals.topic: BaseSandbox.read() UTF-8 boundary detection bug returns base64 for valid text files >8KB
signals.summary: BaseSandbox.read() uses a 8192-byte prefix sniff to decide text vs binary, but UTF-8 is variable-width. When a multi-byte character (CJK, em-dash, accented Latin, emoji) straddles byte 8192, strict decode fails and the entire valid UTF-8 file is returned as base64. The agent silently receives a meaningless base64 blob instead of file contents, breaking any workflow reading text files >8KB (e.g., PDFs, docs).
signals.review_reason: Three independent reports (#2990, #2987, #2983) confirm the same UTF-8 boundary sniff bug in BaseSandbox.read(). This affects any text file over 8KB containing common characters (CJK, em-dashes, curly quotes, accented Latin, emoji) — extremely common in real workflows like reading PDFs or docs. The bug is silent: the agent receives a meaningless base64 blob instead of file contents. One report confirmed it triggered a downstream safety classifier and aborted a multi-hour pipeline, demonstrating real production impact.

source_issues.title: BaseSandbox.read() returns base64 for valid UTF-8 files when multi-byte char straddles 8192-byte sniff boundary
source_issues.evidence: Reproducer confirmed: 9000-byte valid UTF-8 file with em-dash at byte 8190 returns encoding=base64; identical file with em-dash at byte 100 returns encoding=utf-8. Root cause: _READ_COMMAND_TEMPLATE reads first 8192 bytes and calls .decode('utf-8') strictly; if a multi-byte char straddles the boundary, UnicodeDecodeError is raised and the whole file is base64-encoded.

source_issues.title: BaseSandbox.read() returns base64 for valid UTF-8 files when multi-byte char straddles 8192-byte sniff boundary
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed same root cause as #2990. Additional impact: base64 blob fed to model triggered Anthropic usage-policy classifier and aborted a multi-hour pipeline. Inner agent silently received unreadable base64 instead of input file content.

source_issues.title: BaseSandbox.read() returns base64 instead of text for valid UTF-8 files when a multi-byte character is split at the prefix boundary
source_issues.evidence: Same root cause: multi-byte CJK character split at 8192-byte boundary. Reproducer with Korean text (가나다, 3 bytes each) split at boundary. Bug is silent — no exception, just wrong encoding returned.

signals.review_reason: SubAgentMiddleware._run_subagent crashes with IndexError when result['messages'] is an empty list. This is a reproducible crash that blocks the core subagent feature whenever a subagent produces no messages (e.g., early exit, tool-only subagent). Both #3046 (open, with full stack trace) and #3043 (closed, root-cause confirmed) document the same issue independently, confirming real user impact.

Stack trace: 'content = result["messages"][-1].text.rstrip() if result["messages"][-1].text else "" / IndexError: list index out of range'. Subagents are a core feature; any subagent that finishes without emitting messages crashes the parent agent.

signals.topic: deepagents-cli obscures all server-side tracebacks, making errors non-debuggable

signals.review_reason: The CLI's error masking is a widespread debuggability failure: every server-side exception becomes 'An internal error occurred', making filesystem permission problems, symlink loops, missing imports, and network errors indistinguishable. While the specific trigger (#3011 symlink OSError) is separately documented, the CLI debuggability gap means ALL server errors are non-debuggable from the user side, compounding every other error condition.

signals.topic: FilesystemBackend re-raises bare OSError on symlinked SKILL.md, breaking SkillsMiddleware on macOS
signals.summary: FilesystemBackend.download_files doesn't handle bare OSError (e.g., OSError(ELOOP) from symlinked SKILL.md). Since Claude Code's ~/.claude/skills uses symlinks, this aborts agent startup entirely on macOS with SkillsMiddleware enabled (default in deepagents-cli). The underlying errno is stripped by langgraph_api/serde.py, leaving only 'An internal error occurred'.
signals.review_reason: SkillsMiddleware is enabled by default in deepagents-cli, and Claude Code's skill registry (~/.claude/skills) uses symlinks on macOS by design. A single symlinked SKILL.md causes complete agent startup failure with no actionable error. This is a main-flow blocker for macOS users using default configuration, with a clear reproduction path and real-world trigger.

source_issues.title: FilesystemBackend re-raises bare OSError, breaks SkillsMiddleware on symlinked SKILL.md
source_issues.evidence: Reproducer: FilesystemBackend with a symlinked SKILL.md raises OSError(ELOOP) instead of returning FileDownloadResponse(error=...). On macOS, Claude Code's ~/.claude/skills are commonly symlinked. With enable_skills=True (default in deepagents-cli), any such symlink aborts the entire agent: 'RemoteException: {error: OSError, message: An internal error occurred}'. Root cause: _map_exception_to_standard_error only handles specific stdlib subclasses; bare OSError re-raises and tears down the whole batch.

signals.topic: CompositeBackend virtual path mismatch: file ops resolve virtual paths but execute uses literal OS paths
signals.summary: CompositeBackend routes filesystem operations (read/ls/glob/grep) by virtual path prefix, but execute is not path-routable — it always receives the command string verbatim against the default backend's root. When a skill's SKILL.md tells the agent to run 'python /common/skills/yyy/xxx.py', file ops strip the virtual prefix correctly but execute runs the literal '/common/...' path which doesn't exist on the host OS, causing a retry loop.
signals.review_reason: CompositeBackend's virtual path inconsistency is a fundamental design gap: filesystem operations (read/ls/glob/grep) resolve virtual paths, but execute() treats them as literal OS paths. This causes a documented retry loop when agents run skill scripts. The user report from @Smile0524 has a full reproducer with deepagents==0.5.2 and explicit constraints (cloud deployment, unknown root path, skill authors can't hard-code paths), confirming this is a real blocker for skill-based workflows.

source_issues.title: Virtual paths from CompositeBackend routes don't resolve in LocalShellBackend.execute
source_issues.evidence: Converted from user report #2974 (reporter @Smile0524). Reproducer with deepagents==0.5.2: CompositeBackend with routes /common/ and /specified/ mapping to different FilesystemBackends; SKILL.md tells agent to run 'python /common/skills/yyy/xxx.py'. File ops resolve the path (route stripped, mapped to common_path); execute does not — subprocess.run runs literal '/common/...' which doesn't exist at the OS level. Agent probes with ls/grep, gets more virtual paths, reinforcing wrong mental model, producing a retry loop. Confirmed by source: 'execution is not path-routable — it always delegates to the default backend' and 'virtual_mode only affects filesystem operations, not execute()'.

signals.topic: Language.PERL in enum but raises ValueError when used — misleading public API
signals.summary: Language.PERL is listed in the Language enum (line 406 of base.py), signaling to users that Perl is a supported language for code splitting. However, get_separators_for_language() in character.py has no handler for it, causing from_language(Language.PERL) to raise ValueError at runtime.
signals.review_reason: The public enum advertises Language.PERL as a supported option, but using it raises a ValueError. This is a misleading developer experience issue — users discover the feature doesn't exist only at runtime. While count=2, both are duplicate reports from the same author on the same day, suggesting this is a low-frequency but real user-confirmed bug.

signals.topic: Text splitter language separators contain wrong keywords for C# and Elixir — degrades chunking quality

Both are dead separators that never match valid code and silently degrade chunking quality.

signals.topic: HumanInTheLoopMiddleware rejects tool call but ToolNode still executes it — rejection mechanism completely bypassed
signals.summary: When HumanInTheLoopMiddleware processes a 'reject' decision for a tool call, it appends a rejection ToolMessage but fails to remove the tool_call from AIMessage.tool_calls. LangGraph's ToolNode then blindly executes the rejected tool anyway, completely defeating the human-in-the-loop safeguard.
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow-blocking bug: the core safety mechanism (human rejection) is entirely bypassed. A rejected tool is silently executed instead of being prevented. Any user relying on HITL middleware for approval workflows faces uncontrolled tool execution — this defeats the entire purpose of the middleware and constitutes a critical workflow failure.

signals.topic: PostgresStore numeric filter operators use lexicographic comparison causing silently wrong query results
signals.summary: PostgresStore._get_filter_condition() uses text extraction (value->>key) for $gt/$gte/$lt/$lte operators, causing PostgreSQL to perform lexicographic string comparison instead of numeric comparison. This results in silently incorrect query results (e.g., score=9 incorrectly passes a {"score": {"$gte": 10}} filter). The same logic in SqliteStore already uses CAST(... AS REAL) correctly.
signals.review_reason: Silently wrong query results = data corruption. A filter designed to return items with score>=10 incorrectly includes items with score=2-9 because '9' >= '10' in lexicographic ordering. This directly leads to incorrect business logic decisions based on wrong data. High impact + clear reproduction + no workaround.

source_issues.title: Bug: PostgresStore numeric filter operators ($gt, $gte, $lt, $lte) use lexicographic (text) comparison instead of numeric comparison
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible example shows SQL using value->>%s with str param '10' for numeric filters. PostgreSQL text ordering makes '9' >= '10' true. Items with score 2-9 are incorrectly included in $gte:10 results. This silently corrupts query results with no error raised.

signals.topic: BinaryOperatorAggregate.update() silently drops values arriving after Overwrite in same batch
signals.summary: BinaryOperatorAggregate.update() has a guard 'if not seen_overwrite:' that prevents the operator from being applied to values arriving after an Overwrite in the same batch. Values are silently discarded with no error or warning.
signals.review_reason: Silently drops values with no error/warning — data loss that manifests as incorrect graph state. The user has no indication that values were discarded, making debugging extremely difficult. Clear bug with observable behavior.

source_issues.title: bug: BinaryOperatorAggregate.update() silently drops values arriving after Overwrite

signals.topic: PostgresSaver.setup() fails with CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY inside a transaction block
signals.summary: PostgresSaver.setup() raises psycopg.errors.ActiveSqlTransaction when called inside an explicit transaction because CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction block. This breaks atomic provisioning flows where setup() must roll back together with sibling DDL operations.
aliases: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY in transaction block
signals.review_reason: Fails at setup time (P0 blocking) with a hard error that prevents atomic deployment. Users who need transactional rollback of their provisioning cannot use PostgresSaver in any transaction-wrapped deployment flow. This is a deployment-time blocker for production PostgreSQL setups.

The root cause is in ChatResponseUpdateAGUIExtensions.DeserializeResultIfAvailable: it unconditionally attempts to deserialize non-empty tool result content as JsonElement, but plain text content like 'Transferred.' from a handoff fails JSON parsing.
aliases: AGUI SSE event deserialization fails on plain text tool result
signals.review_reason: AGUI is a primary client interface for the framework. The client crashes when processing a valid workflow handoff that produces plain text tool result content — a legitimate and expected scenario. The deserialization is unconditional and not resilient to non-JSON content, which causes a complete client failure.

source_issues.title: .NET: [Bug]: AGUI client crashes on non-JSON TOOL_CALL_RESULT content from handoff with JsonException ('T' is an invalid start of a value)
source_issues.evidence: JsonException thrown in ChatResponseUpdateAGUIExtensions.DeserializeResultIfAvailable when processing TOOL_CALL_RESULT event with plain text content 'Transferred.' from a handoff. Crash occurs in RunStreamingAsync on AGUIChatClient path.

signals.topic: .NET: Microsoft.Agents.AI.GitHub.Copilot incompatible with GitHub.Copilot.SDK 0.3.0 — TypeLoadException on agent run
signals.summary: Microsoft.Agents.AI.GitHub.Copilot 1.3.0-preview.260423.1 is compiled against GitHub.Copilot.SDK 0.1.29. Consumers who need SDK 0.3.0 features (per-session GitHubToken, scoped permissions, sub-agent streaming) hit a TypeLoadException at runtime as soon as the agent attempts to send a message. Several type names were renamed in SDK 0.3.0 (UserMessageDataAttachmentsItem → UserMessageAttachment, etc.), and OnPermissionRequest became a required field.
aliases: TypeLoadException on Copilot agent run with SDK 0.3.0
signals.review_reason: This is a packaging/release incompatibility that blocks consumers from using the GitHub.Copilot integration with the latest SDK. The agent run fails with TypeLoadException, which is a hard runtime failure. The blocked features (per-session GitHubToken, scoped permissions, sub-agent streaming) are primary reasons consumers would use SDK 0.3.0. There is no viable workaround — consumers cannot use the desired SDK version with the current Microsoft.Agents.AI.GitHub.Copilot package.

source_issues.title: .NET: Bump up GitHub.Copilot.SDK to 0.3.0 version
source_issues.evidence: TypeLoadException occurs on UserMessageDataAttachmentsItem/UserMessageDataAttachmentsItemFile types which were renamed in SDK 0.3.0. OnPermissionRequest is now required on SessionConfig. Reporter documents the complete type rename table. PR #5574 was opened fixing all renamed types.

signals.topic: MagenticOne CLI crashes with UnicodeDecodeError for non-English environment users on Windows
signals.summary: playwright_controller.py opens a JS file without specifying encoding='utf-8', causing UnicodeDecodeError ('cp950' codec) when run on Windows systems with non-English locales. The CLI crashes immediately at startup, blocking the entire MagenticOne workflow.
aliases: Non-ASCII file path encoding error in playwright_controller
UTF-8 encoding missing in page_script.js file open call
MagenticOne CLI UnicodeDecodeError on Chinese Windows
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed crash (UnicodeDecodeError) that blocks the MagenticOne CLI startup for all non-English Windows users. The crash occurs at file open in playwright_controller.py when reading page_script.js — without specifying encoding='utf-8', Python defaults to the system encoding (cp950 on Chinese Windows), causing a hard crash. This is a reproducible, user-impacting bug: the tool cannot be used at all by affected users.

source_issues.title: open needs encoding='utf-8' for non-english environment, error in playwright_controller.py
source_issues.evidence: Traceback shows UnicodeDecodeError: 'cp950' codec can't decode byte 0xe2 in position 11569 in playwright_controller.py line 68. User on Chinese Windows (cp950 encoding) runs m1 CLI with Chinese input, crashes immediately. Reproducible: open file without encoding param fails on non-ASCII file content in non-English locale.

signals.topic: TokenLimitedChatCompletionContext truncates from middle of message list instead of oldest messages, causing task logic errors
signals.summary: TokenLimitedChatCompletionContext removes elements from the middle of the conversation history when token limit is reached, instead of removing the oldest messages from the beginning. This can cause critical context (e.g., user instructions, task goals) to be lost while preserving newer but less important messages, leading to incorrect agent behavior.
aliases: Context window truncation removes middle messages instead of oldest
Token truncation strategy causes lost user intent mid-conversation
signals.review_reason: This is a logic error in token management that causes critical context to be silently dropped during multi-turn conversations. When the token limit is hit, middle messages (which may contain original user goals or intermediate decisions) are removed while potentially less important recent messages are kept. This is not a crash but a silent failure: the workflow completes 'successfully' with incorrect or drifting output. The issue is explicitly filed by a user reporting the behavior is wrong.

source_issues.title: TokenLimitedChatCompletionContext removes elements from the middle, which may cause errors in certain situations. Should it remove elements from the beginning of the list rather than from the middle?
source_issues.evidence: Issue explicitly reports that TokenLimitedChatCompletionContext removes from middle of list rather than beginning. Reporter asks whether it 'should remove elements from the beginning of the list rather than from the middle.' Losing middle-context means earlier user goals/instructions can be dropped while keeping later filler messages, leading to agents completing wrong or partial tasks silently.

signals.topic: Import error messages for LLM client dependencies are unhelpful, masking the real cause of failures
signals.summary: When an import error occurs for LLM clients (Anthropic, Gemini, etc.), AutoGen raises a generic hardcoded ImportError message that does not include the actual underlying error (e.g., missing transitive dependencies, version conflicts). Users cannot diagnose why initialization failed, leading to wasted time and inability to use the affected client.
aliases: Generic ImportError hides root cause of LLM client initialization failure
LLM client import error messages lack original error context
signals.review_reason: This is an experience degradation issue: users encounter opaque ImportError messages that mask the true root cause, forcing them to manually trace import chains to find the actual problem. While not a crash, it significantly increases time-to-diagnosis for a critical workflow (LLM client initialization). Closed with 'good first issue' label, indicating it's a recognized legitimate bug. Count=1 so P2 is appropriate.

source_issues.title: Improve Import Error Messages for LLM Client Dependencies
source_issues.evidence: Issue shows actual vs. expected error message: when vertexai import fails, user sees 'Please install google-generativeai' while actual error was 'No module named vertexai'. The misleading message prevents users from understanding the real dependency issue. 18 comments indicate community interest.

signals.topic: Missing group chat message thread access API in BaseGroupChat
signals.summary: Users cannot retrieve the current message thread from a group chat team via a public API. The conversation history is only accessible internally, making it impossible to inspect, audit, or resume group chat state from outside the team — blocking integration scenarios and observability.
aliases: Cannot access group chat conversation history externally
No public API to get group chat message history
signals.review_reason: Key functionality (accessing group chat message history externally) is unavailable through any public API. Users must use internal mechanisms or workarounds. This blocks observability, audit, and integration scenarios. While it's a feature request, the inability to inspect group chat state is a functional gap affecting production use cases. Count=1 so P2 is appropriate.

source_issues.title: Get current message thread from a group chat team.
source_issues.evidence: Issue explicitly requests a public method to get all messages that have happened so far in BaseGroupChat via async send_message. Requires new GroupChatGetThread RPC event type. Currently no public API exists, blocking external state inspection. 7 comments indicate community demand.

signals.topic: No LLM tracing support for create_stream API, breaking observability for streaming completions
signals.summary: AutoGen traces LLM calls for the synchronous create API but not for the create_stream (streaming) API. Agents using streaming completions have zero observability coverage — no spans, no token counts, no latency metrics — making it impossible to debug or optimize streaming workflows.
signals.review_reason: Streaming LLM calls have no observability coverage in AutoGen's tracing system. For production deployments using streaming (a common pattern), users cannot see token usage, latency, or spans for those calls — making debugging and optimization impossible. This is a functional gap for a key capability (streaming), not a blocker but a significant observability deficit.

source_issues.title: Trace LLM call spans for both create and create_stream
source_issues.evidence: Issue explicitly requests tracing support for both create and create_stream LLM APIs. Currently only synchronous create is instrumented. Streaming is a key use case in production; lack of tracing means zero observability for streaming agent workflows.

signals.topic: BiDi protocol regressions break proxy support and file downloads
signals.summary: Two regressions (#40493 and #40495) broke core BiDi functionality: proxy support via browserType.connect() and file downloads. Existing tests fail, indicating these are not edge cases.
signals.review_reason: 两个回归问题均标记为Regression标签，且都有内置测试失败作为直接证据。proxy和download是浏览器自动化的核心功能，BiDi协议用户受影响面广，不是边缘场景。虽然count=2未达3，但两条issue都是明确的主流程阻断+有测试代码支撑，符合P0的核心条件。

source_issues.title: [Regression]: #40493 breaks proxy support in BiDi with browserType.connect()
source_issues.evidence: Run 'should proxy localhost requests' in tests/library/browsertype-connect.spec.ts fails after #40493 was merged. Proxy support is a core remote browser feature.

source_issues.title: [Regression]: #40495 breaks downloads with BiDi
source_issues.evidence: Tests in tests/library/download.spec.ts fail after #40495, including 'should save downloads to artifactsDir'. Downloads are a fundamental browser automation capability.

signals.topic: Firefox pointer/hover events fail in parallel page execution
signals.summary: Pointer events (hover, tooltip triggers) only work on 1 out of N pages when multiple Firefox pages run in parallel. Works correctly in series or in Chromium/Safari.
aliases: Firefox pointer events flaky parallel pages
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：Firefox是Playwright三大主力浏览器之一，并行测试是核心用例。用户提供了可复现代码，现象明确（5个并行页面中只有1个的hover生效），在非Firefox浏览器上完全正常。这不是边缘场景，而是影响Firefox用户并行测试能力的直接阻断问题。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Pointer events don't work in Firefox in parallel
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible test case shows pointer events only work in 1 of 5 pages during parallel execution on Firefox; works in Chromium and Safari. Previously reported in #27517 (closed for lack of bandwidth). Blocks parallel test suites targeting Firefox, a primary browser target.

signals.topic: WebKit WebInspector displays black screen in Playwright 1.59
signals.summary: Opening developer tools (F12) on WebKit via Playwright shows only a black screen, making WebKit dev tools completely unusable. Regression from 1.58.2.
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用：WebInspector是WebKit上开发者调试的核心工具，1.59版本完全黑屏意味着WebKit的devtools调试路径被彻底阻断。明确标记为regression，Chromium/Firefox不受影响，指向Playwright 1.59对WebKit的引入的破坏。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: WebInspector in WebKit in Playwright 1.59 doesn't work - a black screen is displayed
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible with 'npx playwright wk https://playwright.dev' then F12. Black screen appears. Works in 1.58.2, broken in 1.59. Chromium/Firefox unaffected. Blocks WebKit developer tools debugging entirely.

signals.topic: CLI trace snapshot command hangs in infinite loop with nested iframes
signals.summary: The 'playwright trace snapshot' CLI command hangs indefinitely with timeout instead of outputting snapshot data, caused by incorrect iframe URL base path concatenation in enterprise micro-frontend pages.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：trace snapshot CLI是trace调试的常用命令行路径，对于复杂页面（企业微前端场景，多层嵌套iframe）完全不可用，超时30秒而非输出结果。用户提供了DEBUG日志证明无限导航循环，不是偶发问题。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: CLI trace snapshot hangs in infinite loop due to chaotic iframe path concatenation (+ Feature Request: Trace Sanitization)
source_issues.evidence: CLI command hangs at 30000ms timeout. Debug logs show infinite 'navigated to' loop with malformed iframe URLs like 'frame@xxx/frame@yyy/frame@yyy'. Trace viewer UI works but CLI is completely broken for complex pages. Enterprise users with micro-frontend dashboards blocked from CLI-based trace debugging.

signals.topic: MCP extension mode ignores explicit executable path, breaking non-default browser/profile targeting
signals.summary: When using Playwright MCP in extension mode, the --executable-path CLI flag and PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_EXECUTABLE_PATH env var are ignored, causing the relay to open in the wrong browser. MCP requests fail with error -32001.
aliases: MCP extension mode executable path ignored
signals.review_reason: MCP扩展模式的核心功能失效：用户明确指定了要使用的浏览器可执行文件和用户数据目录，但被忽略。这对于WSL/CDE等非默认浏览器使用场景是阻断性的，用户的所有MCP请求都会超时失败。issue提供了根因分析和修复方案，表明这是一个确定的代码缺陷。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Playwright MCP extension mode ignores explicit executable path
source_issues.evidence: WSL/CDE user with Windows Edge profile: explicit --executable-path is ignored, relay opens in Linux Edge instead. MCP requests time out with -32001 'Request timed out' and 'Not connected' errors. Root cause identified in source: extensionContextFactory.ts not passing executablePath to CDPRelayServer. Has 1 comment confirming the issue.

signals.topic: Python Redis connector: multiple critical bugs causing data loss, vector search failure, and index corruption
signals.summary: Three independent bugs in the Python Redis connector all cause data integrity or functional failures: (1) RedisJsonCollection.delete() silently fails to delete records when prefix_collection_name_to_key_names is enabled (upsert stores keys as 'prefix:key' but delete sends 'key' without prefix); (2) FT.SEARCH vector search completely broken due to TypeError in StorageType vs IndexSchema mismatch and KeyError on missing vector field; (3) FT.CREATE sends PREFIX as one character per element instead of the full collection name string, corrupting index definition.
aliases: Python Redis connector data integrity bugs
signals.review_reason: Three bugs from the same Python Redis connector codebase all produce observable user-impacting failures: data that users believe is deleted remains in Redis, vector search is completely broken with unhandled exceptions, and index creation silently creates malformed indexes. These are not edge cases — they directly block users from using SK's Redis storage capabilities. All three have wire-capture evidence and clear root cause analysis.

source_issues.title: Python: Bug: RedisJsonCollection.delete() silently fails when prefix_collection_name_to_key_names is enabled
source_issues.evidence: Wire capture shows JSON.SET with prefix 'sk_cov_xxx:cov-1' but JSON.DEL without prefix 'cov-1'. Record is never deleted; subsequent get still returns the record. Root cause identified as missing _get_redis_key() call. Affects data integrity.

source_issues.title: Python: Bug: Vector search (FT.SEARCH) via the Python Redis connector is broken
source_issues.evidence: Every FT.SEARCH call raises AttributeError: 'StorageType' object has no attribute 'index' due to API mismatch with redisvl 0.15.0. Secondary KeyError on missing vector field when include_vectors=False. Core vector search feature is completely non-functional.

source_issues.title: Python: Bug: Redis connector sends malformed FT.CREATE PREFIX (one prefix per character of collection name)
source_issues.evidence: Wire capture shows FT.CREATE sending 'PREFIX 27 r e d i s _ j s o n _ l i s t _ d a t a _ m o d e l :' instead of 'PREFIX 1 redis_json_list_data_model:'. Index creation is silently corrupted; bugs #13896 and #13904 are downstream consequences.

signals.topic: .NET Orchestration: ReasoningEffort setting silently lost during agent invocation, breaking main agent reasoning flow
signals.summary: In .NET SK, the ReasoningEffort parameter set on an agent is lost when that agent is used inside an orchestration (e.g. HandOff). The HTTP request sent to the LLM is missing the reasoning_effort field, so the model falls back to default reasoning regardless of the agent's configured effort level.
aliases: .NET reasoning effort not preserved in HandOff
signals.review_reason: Two independent reports confirm that .NET users' configured ReasoningEffort is silently dropped during orchestration invocation. This is a main-flow failure: users explicitly configure reasoning effort and the model silently falls back to default behavior without any error. With two reports including an actively discussed thread (10 comments), this represents clear user impact on core functionality.

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: Semantic Kernel Orchestration: ReasoningEffort setting becomes lost when invoking
source_issues.evidence: User sets GPT-5.4 with ReasoningEffort='high', creates HandOff orchestration, invokes it, and observes HTTP request is missing the reasoning_effort field entirely. Affects main agent workflow.

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: chat/completions no reasoning
source_issues.evidence: Active user discussion (10 comments) confirming reasoning not working in chat/completions for .NET. Open issue with triage label, clearly user-impacting.

signals.topic: MCP tool integration accepts and trusts server-supplied tool definitions without integrity verification — tool poisoning attack surface
signals.summary: When Semantic Kernel loads MCP tools via MCPPluginBase.load_tools(), tool names, descriptions, and parameter schemas are accepted directly from the MCP server with no verification. Combined with auto-invocation, a compromised or malicious MCP server can inject directives into tool descriptions that the LLM treats as system instructions, or silently replace tool definitions mid-session via notifications/tools/list_changed. Research shows 72.8% attack success rate across 20 LLM agents.
signals.review_reason: While only one issue report, this describes a real, published security vulnerability class with CVEs and benchmark evidence. The attack surface is not theoretical — there are documented supply chain attacks (postmark-mcp) and published CVEs. When SK users connect to an MCP server with auto-invocation enabled, a malicious server can exfiltrate data, manipulate agent behavior, or escalate privileges without requiring any additional exploit. The single report is well-documented with external CVEs and research. This warrants P1 rather than P0 due to single-source count and the fact that the attack requires a compromised MCP server (an external dependency).

source_issues.title: MCP tool integration trusts server-supplied definitions without integrity verification
source_issues.evidence: Tool descriptions are injected into LLM context unsanitised, message_handler silently reloads tools on notifications/tools/list_changed, no schema pinning, sampling callback passes server-supplied systemPrompt directly to LLM. Referenced: CVE-2025-6514 (CVSS 9.6), CVE-2025-49596 (CVSS 9.4), postmark-mcp supply chain attack. 72.8% attack success rate in MCPTox benchmark. OWASP MCP-01.

signals.topic: Python: Azure Monitor telemetry instrumentation breaks AgentGroupChat multi-agent workflows with ValueError
signals.summary: When Azure Monitor (configure_azure_monitor) is enabled, using AzureAIAgent inside AgentGroupChat causes all agent executions to fail with 'ValueError: Unknown response format <class 'dict'>'. The Azure AI telemetry instrumentor does not support dict type response_format and raises ValueError during thread/run creation, breaking the multi-agent execution flow entirely.
signals.review_reason: Users who have enabled Azure Monitor for production telemetry cannot use AgentGroupChat — a core multi-agent orchestration feature. The failure is immediate and unrecoverable, affecting the complete agent execution pipeline. This creates a forced choice between telemetry and multi-agent functionality. While closed, it represents a real incompatibility that blocks users from combining observability tooling with multi-agent workflows.

source_issues.title: Bug: [Python] AgentGroupChat fails with 'Unknown response format <class 'dict'>' when Azure Monitor is enabled
source_issues.evidence: AgentGroupChat with AzureAIAgent fails immediately on tool invocation. Automatic retries occur but all fail with the same ValueError. The instrumentor intercepts thread/run creation calls and raises on dict type response_format. Multi-agent workflow is completely blocked. Reported with specific package versions including azure-monitor-opentelemetry 1.8.6, opentelemetry-sdk 1.39.0.

signals.topic: .NET: NotSupportedException thrown when logging function results involving MCP plugin tools with TextContent
signals.summary: In .NET SK, when MCP plugins (via ModelContextProtocol.AspNetCore) are added to the kernel and SK logging is enabled, every function result triggers a NotSupportedException in LogFunctionResultValueInternal. The serialization fails because JsonTypeInfo for Microsoft.Extensions.AI.TextContent is not registered in the SK JSON context, causing error logs to appear on every tool call.
aliases: SK logging NotSupportedException with MCP plugins
signals.review_reason: This is a clear user pain point — every MCP tool invocation produces a NotSupportedException in logs, cluttering production logs with errors. While the author notes it doesn't block execution, error logs on every call degrade observability and signal to users that something is wrong. The exception is thrown by SK's own logging code, not an external library, making this a legitimate SK bug. It is P2 rather than P1 because: single report, execution is not blocked, and the symptom is purely logging-side.

source_issues.title: Bug: NotImplementedException on SK Logging
source_issues.evidence: Every MCP tool invocation produces a NotSupportedException in the log when SK logging is enabled. Error message: 'JsonTypeInfo metadata for type Microsoft.Extensions.AI.TextContent was not provided by TypeInfoResolver'. Occurs on .NET SK 1.73.0 with ModelContextProtocol.AspNetCore 1.1.0.

signals.topic: Windows platform: Settings crash, Browser plugin DOM/screenshot APIs broken, CLI silent exit, plugin discovery blocked by Cloudflare 403
signals.summary: Four separate Windows-specific issues collectively render the Windows platform largely unusable: Settings crashes on null reference, Browser plugin cannot start app-server (Access is denied), CLI exits silently with exit code 0xC0000135 when VC++ Redistributable missing, and MCP/plugin discovery returns Cloudflare 403 challenge HTML instead of API JSON.
aliases: Windows Browser plugin cannot start app-server
Windows CLI silent exit missing VC++ Redistributable
signals.review_reason: count=4 with sample links: Windows platform-wide failures blocking Settings, CLI, Browser plugin, and plugin discovery simultaneously. All four have clear error evidence (null reference crash, Access is denied, silent 0xC0000135 exit, Cloudflare 403 HTML responses). Systemic Windows platform compatibility failure.

source_issues.title: Windows app Settings crashes when external agent import panel renders (path.win32 is null)
source_issues.evidence: Settings crashes with TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'dirname') when path.win32 is null. Blocks Settings access entirely on Windows.

source_issues.title: Windows Codex app: Browser plugin can attach to tab, but DOM/screenshot APIs fail because codex app-server cannot start
source_issues.evidence: Browser plugin DOM snapshot, screenshot, visible DOM APIs fail with 'failed to start codex app-server: Access is denied'. codex.exe and node_repl.exe cannot be launched from integrated PowerShell under MSIX package.

source_issues.title: Windows: codex fails silently without Visual C++ Redistributable installed
source_issues.evidence: codex CLI exits with 0xC0000135 (STATUS_DLL_NOT_FOUND) silently when VC++ Redistributable is missing. No error message. CLI completely unusable.

source_issues.title: mcp-search fails after clean reinstall on Windows: ChatGPT backend plugin/connectors requests return Cloudflare 403
source_issues.evidence: Remote plugin/app discovery requests to chatgpt.com/backend-api/plugins/... return 403 Forbidden with Cloudflare challenge HTML. MCP initialization fails at handshake. Settings UI breaks. Entire plugin ecosystem unavailable even after clean reinstall.

signals.topic: Computer Use crashes and Browser Use / Google Sheets connector failures blocking core automation features
signals.summary: Three issues blocking automation workflows: Computer Use crashes SkyComputerUseService with SIGBUS/excessive recursion when inspecting Outlook on macOS; Browser Use cannot connect to IAB backend from Node REPL tool; Google Sheets connector fails with AttributeError (_connector missing).
aliases: Browser Use IAB connection failure Node REPL
signals.review_reason: count=3 with sample links: all three are core automation features (Computer Use, Browser Use, Google Sheets) blocked by crashes or clear AttributeError/connection failures. Main workflow interruption with direct user impact.

source_issues.title: Computer Use crashes SkyComputerUseService when inspecting Outlook on macOS
source_issues.evidence: SkyComputerUseService crashes with EXC_BAD_ACCESS/SIGBUS and stack exhaustion when get_app_state is called for Outlook. Blocks Outlook desktop automation entirely.

source_issues.title: Browser Use cannot connect to IAB from Node REPL on macOS

source_issues.title: Google Drive Sheets connector fails with AttributeError: GoogleSheetsConnector._connector missing
source_issues.evidence: Google Sheets connector fails with AttributeError: GoogleSheetsConnector has no attribute '_connector'. Spreadsheet metadata tools completely broken.

signals.topic: UI rendering failures: code-comment blocks not rendering, Branch Details overlay blocking send/stop buttons
signals.summary: Two UI rendering issues: code-comment blocks sometimes fail to render (blank area shown with screenshot evidence), and the Branch Details popup overlays and blocks mouse interactions on the send/stop buttons.
signals.review_reason: count=2: two distinct UI rendering failures with visual evidence. Branch Details overlay directly blocks send/stop button — user action is suppressed. Code block rendering gap causes visible content to disappear. Both are clear UX degradation.

source_issues.title: Code-comment block not rendering properly
source_issues.evidence: Code comment block does not render in some sessions. Screenshot shows blank area where code block should appear. User-facing content is missing.

source_issues.title: Codex Desktop: Branch Details Blocking Stop & Send Buttons

signals.topic: Session replay poisoned after context compaction emits malformed tool_search_call — entire session becomes permanently unusable
signals.summary: After context compaction, Codex Desktop persists a malformed tool_search_call with a 1582-char junk property name into the session transcript. signals.review_reason: Single-issue P0: complete session workflow blockage with explicit API error evidence (400 property_name_above_max_length). This is a main-flow failure that permanently breaks all future retries of the session.

source_issues.title: Codex Desktop session replay is poisoned after compaction emits malformed tool_search_call arguments
source_issues.evidence: Malformed tool_search_call with 1582-char property name persisted after context_compacted event. Session replay fails with API 400 property_name_above_max_length on input[184].arguments. Session completely unusable until manual JSONL editing.

signals.topic: MCP tool names from OpenAI-compatible proxies fail strict resolution — all MCP tools unusable with non-GPT models
signals.summary: When using Codex with Ollama, Bifrost, or LiteLLM proxies, MCP tools registered under namespaces (e.g. mcp__tilth__) cannot be called because Codex's resolve_mcp_tool_info performs strict equality checks. aliases: MCP tool name resolution failure OpenAI-compatible proxy
Ollama MCP tools unsupported call error

source_issues.title: Resolution failure for flattened MCP tool names from OpenAI-compatible proxies
source_issues.evidence: MCP tools under namespace fail resolution when proxy flattens names to mcp__server__tool pattern. McpConnectionManager::resolve_mcp_tool_info performs strict equality check. Results in 'unsupported call' error. All MCP tools unusable with Ollama/LiteLLM.

signals.topic: RealtimeAgent工具调用在响应进行中时触发create.response导致agent卡死

RealtimeAgent stuck waiting for customer request after tool call
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：agent被卡住无法继续，必须等用户下一次请求才恢复。5条评论，v0.14.2生产环境确认，持续活跃(open状态)。在并发/异步工具调用场景下必现，影响实时对话体验。

source_issues.title: Realtime Tools cause agent response to cut off

signals.topic: Model refusals with structured output导致agent陷入无限重试循环
signals.summary: 当API返回refusal且使用了structured output时，ItemHelpers.extract_text()忽略refusal导致无文本返回，SDK陷入重试循环直到max_turns耗尽，消耗额外API调用和token费用。
aliases: Refusal loops until max_turns with structured output

signals.topic: UnixLocal PTY子进程继承父进程SIGINT处置，Ctrl-C无法中断长运行任务

aliases: PTY child inherits parent SIGINT ignoring, Ctrl-C doesn't work
UnixLocal PTY exec process can't be interrupted when parent ignores SIGINT
signals.review_reason: Sandbox功能部分阻断：PTY模式下无法通过Ctrl-C中断长运行任务，用户需用其他方式终止进程，影响交互式sandbox使用体验。根因明确，但触发条件相对特殊(count=1)。

source_issues.title: Bug: UnixLocal PTY children can inherit ignored SIGINT and miss Ctrl-C interrupts
source_issues.evidence: preexec_fn未在exec前将SIGINT重置为SIG_DFL，导致PTY子进程的Ctrl-C中断行为依赖于父进程当前信号处置。提供复现步骤：设置父进程SIGINT为SIG_IGN后启动PTY子进程，写入\x03子进程保持运行而非退出。

signals.topic: Async Responses Structured Outputs causes unbounded memory leak leading to OOM
signals.summary: openai/lib/_parsing/_responses.py calls construct_type_unchecked with TypeVar-subscripted generics (ParsedResponse[TextFormatT]). Since TextFormatT is unresolved, pydantic's model_rebuild always fails and MockCoreSchema._built_memo is never populated, causing a new SchemaValidator/SchemaSerializer to be allocated on every responses.parse() call. Long-running servers accumulate unbounded Rust objects until OOM.
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed SDK bug causing unbounded memory growth in long-running servers. Each responses.parse() call allocates heavy Rust objects (SchemaValidator/SchemaSerializer) that are never freed. Evidence includes flame graph profiling and clear root-cause analysis. Leads directly to OOM in production — a critical reliability failure for server workloads.

source_issues.title: Async Responses Structured Outputs Memory leak
source_issues.evidence: Flame graph attached showing pydantic schema rebuild accumulation. RSS grows linearly with request count in long-running server. Root cause: construct_type_unchecked with TypeVar-subscripted generics causes model_rebuild(raise_errors=False) to always return False, preventing cache population.

signals.topic: PydanticUserError in multiprocess forkserver workers with defer_build=True and pydantic 2.12
signals.summary: When using pydantic 2.12 with DEFER_PYDANTIC_BUILD=true (default) in multiprocess forkserver environments (~700 workers), 0.6-9.5% of requests fail intermittently with 'Pydantic models should inherit from BaseModel, BaseModel cannot be instantiated directly'. The hardcoded _parent_namespace_depth=5 walks up the call stack and misses the openai types namespace, causing model_rebuild to fail silently.
signals.review_reason: Intermittent but reproducible request failures (0.6-9.5%) in production multiprocess environments with large worker counts. Blocks a significant fraction of requests when running high-throughput workloads. Root cause is clearly traced to pydantic's namespace depth assumption being violated in forkserver context.

source_issues.title: PydanticUserError with defer_build=True and pydantic 2.12 in multiprocess forkserver workers
source_issues.evidence: 0.6% error rate with DEFER_PYDANTIC_BUILD=true in production with ~700 forkserver workers processing millions of requests. Error rate rises to 9.5% with DEFER_PYDANTIC_BUILD=false. Full stack trace from openai/_models.py construct() through _get_extra_fields_type() to MockCoreSchema._get_built(). Related to pydantic/pydantic#11849 race condition.

signals.topic: vector_stores.files.upload_and_poll() hangs indefinitely with no error when file processing is stuck at in_progress

signals.topic: WebView2 native↔SPA bidirectional bridge missing, causing fragile DOM-scraping workarounds in voice and screen recording features
signals.summary: The Windows node has no formal WebView2 bridge for native↔SPA communication. Voice mode (#120) and screen recording work around this with DOM scraping (querySelector/MutationObserver hacks) described as 'fragile' by their own authors. This fragile state affects multiple features and risks breaking silently.
signals.review_reason: Multiple production features (voice mode, screen recording, canvas window) rely on fragile DOM-scraping hacks because the WebView2 bridge is missing. The #120 author explicitly labels the workaround 'fragile' and #191 catalogs that 11 heuristic fallbacks exist in CanvasWindow with no proper alternative. This is a known reliability and maintenance problem affecting user-facing features, not a hypothetical risk.

source_issues.title: [Proposal] Add a formal WebView2 bridge for native ↔ SPA communication

signals.topic: Windows packaging ambiguity: three install formats (EXE/ZIP/MSIX) with inconsistent in-app auto-update behavior
signals.summary: Windows tray ships via Inno Setup installer, portable ZIP (wired to Updatum auto-updater), and MSIX — but the auto-updater may accidentally update an MSIX install with ZIP files or an installer install with incompatible portable layout. Users may cross install technologies during update unintentionally.
signals.review_reason: Packaging ambiguity creates a real risk of silent update failures where users install via one format (EXE) but auto-updater serves another format (ZIP/MSIX), potentially breaking the installation. This is not purely theoretical — the issue author explicitly identifies this as a blocker for 'broader distribution.' However count=1 and it is not yet causing active user failures, so P2 is appropriate.

source_issues.title: Decide Windows packaging and auto-update strategy
source_issues.evidence: App code configures Updatum for portable/single-file update flow but installer also exists; MSIX has its own update semantics disconnected from Updatum. Clear documented risk: 'updater does not accidentally update an MSIX install with ZIP files or an installer install with an incompatible portable layout.' Active decision needed before broader distribution.

aliases: Remote code execution via auto_run toggle
signals.review_reason: 安全关键词关联且有明确技术证据：端点接受用户消息内容中的 {AUTO_RUN_ON} 直接控制 auto_run 布尔值，在默认配置（无 INTERPRETER_REQUIRE_AUTH）下可被任意远程客户端利用，实现自动代码执行。虽然 count=1，但该漏洞影响默认配置下的所有部署实例，严重程度高，需保留。
